records.description: The Ibrahim Leadership Fellowships place three Fellows per year for 12 months in the executive offices of the African Development Bank (Abidjan), the UN Economic Commission for Africa (Addis Ababa) or the International Trade Centre (Geneva). Fellows work on research and policy design and receive direct mentorship from the head of the host organisation. The Mo Ibrahim Foundation funds the position; the Foundation's own programme page states a stipend of $100,000. This is a professional work placement, not a degree-granting scholarship, so no tuition is paid.
records.best_fit: African nationals with a master's degree and at least seven years of relevant work experience who want senior-level policy exposure in a continental or multilateral institution.
records.eligibility_summary: Nationals of any African country with a minimum master's degree, at least seven years of relevant work experience, and under 40 (45 for women with children).

records.selection_notes: The host's Human Resources department vets applications to draw up a shortlist of ten files, which the Foundation then reviews; a shortlist of three candidates is put to the head of the host (for the AfDB route, the President of the Bank or a designate) for final selection. Only applicants who fully meet the requirements and are considered for interview are contacted.
records.notes: This is a work placement, not a degree programme: the contract is for one (1) year and is not renewable, and the Fellow is not a regular employee of the host and gains no right to employment. For the AfDB route the Fellow is barred from applying for a staff position at the Bank for one year from the end of the Fellowship. The Fellow is not eligible for the Bank's child educational scheme, staff medical insurance or retirement plans; the Mo Ibrahim Foundation is responsible for ensuring the Fellow arranges their own medical insurance, child education and retirement plan. Applications are routed through three different host systems with potentially different closing dates, so check the host page you intend to use.

official_details.citizenship_residency: Nationals of an African country. AfDB route additionally requires nationality of an AfDB member country and states the candidate may reside anywhere in the world.
purpose: Identify and mentor the future generation of outstanding African leaders. The Ibrahim Leadership Fellowships were established in 2011 for this purpose (Mo Ibrahim Foundation fellowships page).

Prepare the next generation of outstanding African leaders by providing unique work opportunities at the most senior level of prominent African institutions or multilateral organizations whose mandate is to improve the economic and social prospects of Africa, thereby creating a pipeline of future African leaders (AfDB vacancy notice).
Allow talented individuals to increase and enhance their professional capacity with the intention of contributing to the governance and development of their countries (AfDB vacancy notice).

Enable young African professionals to develop leadership capacity in a large institution, gain knowledge of the functioning of the United Nations, better understand Africa's socio-economic challenges and contribute to the analytical, advocacy and policy advisory work of the Commission (UNECA 2027 Mo Ibrahim Fellowship Programme notice).
sdg_requirement_details: No SDG or development-alignment requirement is published for applicants. The UNECA notice states that ECA's mission is informed by the 2030 Agenda and Agenda 2063 and lists ECA's five strategic directions (including green growth, innovative financing for infrastructure, peace and security, and gender equality), but it does not require applicants to align their proposal with, or report against, any specific SDG.
The Mo Ibrahim Foundation's own fellowships page attaches no development or SDG designation to the Fellowship.
study_type: Professional work placement / leadership fellowship in the executive office of an international institution
Research and policy design assignment, not a taught course of study
official_details.degree_award: None. The Fellowship is a 12-month funded work placement. No degree, certificate or academic credit is awarded by the Foundation or by the host organisation on any official page read.
official_details.tuition_rule: Not applicable. No tuition is charged and none is waived, because no course of study is funded. The AfDB notice states that the Foundation 'will finance the costs associated with the position' and that 'this position is not a regular position of the African Development Bank'.
covered_expenses: Annual stipend of $100,000, paid monthly by the host organisation out of funds provided by the Foundation (AfDB: 'The fellow will receive an annual stipend monthly paid by the Bank out of the funds provided by Foundation')

All expenses related to the Fellow's official mission travel, including travel insurance, borne by the host organisation but excluding assumption-of-duty and repatriation travel (AfDB and UNECA notices)
Travel and shipping costs for the assumption of duty and repatriation at the end of the appointment, borne and paid out of funds provided by the Foundation (AfDB and UNECA notices)
Invitation to the Foundation's annual Forum (UNECA notice: 'The Foundation will invite the Fellow to participate in its annual Forum')
not_covered_or_excluded: The host's child educational scheme: 'The Fellow shall not participate in the Bank's child educational scheme' (AfDB notice)

The host's staff medical insurance and retirement plans: the Fellow 'shall not participate in the Bank's staff medical insurance and retirement plans' (AfDB notice; UNECA notice states the same exclusion)

The Fellow's own medical insurance, child education and retirement plan arrangements: 'The Fellow will cover his/her own medical insurance, child education and retirement plan arrangements for the period he/she will be working at ECA' (UNECA notice); the Foundation's role is only to ensure the Fellow has such arrangements (AfDB notice)
Any tuition, course or study cost of any kind
Any remuneration, pension or employee benefit beyond the published stipend: no such entitlement is published
Housing, meals and general living costs: no official page itemises these, so they are not established as covered
general_eligibility: National of an African country (Mo Ibrahim Foundation fellowships page). AfDB route: must be a national of an AfDB member country, residing anywhere in the world. UNECA route: must be a national of an ECA member State, residing anywhere in the world.
At least 7 years of relevant work experience (Foundation page, AfDB notice and UNECA notice all state this).

Master's degree as a minimum: the Foundation page states 'Master's degree'; the AfDB notice requires 'outstanding academic credentials backed by a minimum of a Master's Degree from a recognized institution in banking, business, economics or other social sciences, finance, international development, or in any other discipline relevant to the Bank's business'; the UNECA notice requires 'at least a Master's degree or higher in Economics, Social Sciences, International Development, Business Administration, Law, Finance, Engineering, or any discipline relevant to the work of ECA'.

Under the age of 40; 45 for women with children (Foundation page and AfDB notice). For UNECA, under 40 on the date of the application deadline (20 November 2026), with consideration given to women under 45 with children on that date.
Relevant and demonstrable work experience, strong communication skills, demonstrated leadership skills and the ability to work with others (AfDB notice).
Competency in professionalism, teamwork, client orientation, planning and organising, and leadership potential (UNECA notice).
Sound knowledge of the internet and basic software for word processing, spreadsheets and presentations (UNECA notice).
UNECA route only: fluency in either English or French, with working knowledge of the other language desirable, and the application must be in either English or French.
ineligibility_conditions: Not an active, non-active, retired or separated staff member of the African Development Bank (AfDB route)
No close family relations with an active or non-active staff member of the Bank, such as mother, father, sister and brother (AfDB route)
Government officials, active military personnel and political party leaders are not eligible (AfDB route)
Not a national of an AfDB member country (AfDB route: 'To apply for this position, you need to be national of one of AfDB member countries')
Must not be an employee of the United Nations Secretariat or ECA (UNECA route)
Aged 40 or over on the application deadline date, unless the applicant is a woman under 45 with children (UNECA route)
Applications received after 20 November 2026 at 11:59 p.m. (23:59) Addis Ababa time are not reviewed, and 'no exceptions will be made' (UNECA route)
Incomplete submissions are not considered 'under any circumstances'; where several submissions are received from the same applicant only the most recent is reviewed (UNECA route)

masters: A Master's degree is the minimum academic qualification on all three host routes. AfDB: 'outstanding academic credentials backed by a minimum of a Master's Degree'. UNECA: 'at least a Master's degree or higher'. The Mo Ibrahim Foundation's own page states only 'Master's degree'.

The AfDB notice additionally requires the discipline to be relevant to the Bank's business; the UNECA notice lists Economics, Social Sciences, International Development, Business Administration, Law, Finance, Engineering or any discipline relevant to the work of ECA.
phd: No separate PhD-level rule is published for the 2027 cycle. The UNECA notice requires 'at least a Master's degree or higher', so a doctorate satisfies the education minimum, but no additional academic standard is set for PhD holders and no doctoral funding is described.

host_requirements: AfDB route: the Fellow performs the functions and duties of the position at the headquarters of the Bank in Abidjan, Republic of Côte d'Ivoire, 'or in any other location from which the Bank carries out its operations'.
AfDB route: the Fellow takes leadership guidance from the President, the Managing Directors, the Chief of Staff and Director of Cabinet and/or a designated Representative.

UNECA route: duty station Addis Ababa, Ethiopia; the Fellow is mentored by the Executive Secretary of ECA and/or a designated Representative in the Office of the Executive Secretary (OES) and supports the OES programmatic and administrative functions.
ITC route: the Foundation's page quotes the ITC Executive Director describing the programme as an opportunity to work alongside the Executive Director and her team in Geneva.
The Fellow signs a contract with the host before commencing of service (AfDB and UNECA notices).

For the duration of the contract the Fellow must comply with the Staff Regulations and Rules of the host for all operational purposes and purposes of conduct, and only the host, not the Foundation, may direct and instruct the Fellow.
The Fellow may be required to travel to different locations on the host's instructions (AfDB notice).

For the AfDB route, the host's own recruitment system applies the same standards as staff recruitment, including that the Bank does not accept dual nationality and requires supporting government-issued IDs such as a passport or national identity card.
document_format_rules: UNECA route: all documents must be submitted as PDF attachments. The notice states 'any other document/attachment types will not be accepted'.
UNECA route: large documents may be combined or compressed into a .zip file if necessary. The notice states 'Please do NOT use any other file compression formats (e.g. RAR)'.
UNECA route: the application must be in either English or French.
UNECA route: all required documents must be submitted at one time and in one email; the notice states that only the most recent submission from an applicant will be reviewed.

UNECA route: the UN Administrative Profile (AP) must be generated as a PDF from the Inspira system (https://inspira.un.org) and attached to the email. The notice states that ECA does not have the ability to retrieve draft or created APs from Inspira, so an email submission without a complete AP as a PDF attachment is considered incomplete and will not be reviewed.

UNECA route: the cover/motivation letter is created inside the online AP creation process in Inspira and appears on page 1 of the AP PDF under the heading 'Cover Letter/Motivation Statement for this Application'.
UNECA route: take a screenshot showing that the online survey responses have been sent, and include it in PDF format.

UNECA route: letters of recommendation must be addressed to the '2027 ECA Mo Ibrahim Leadership Fellow Selection Committee'. Referees must send the letters directly to the applicant, who then includes them in the email submission; letters transmitted directly from referees to ECA will not be considered.

UNECA route: copies of academic degree certificates for master's degrees and doctorate/terminal degrees only. The notice states that copies of academic certificates that are not degrees, and copies of high school diplomas/transcripts, are not required, and that first-level (baccalaureate) documentation is not required because a master's is the minimum.

AfDB route: the online form on the Bank's website must be completed and submitted with a comprehensive CV indicating date of birth, nationality, education and relevant experience, plus copies of academic transcripts and three letters of recommendation attached.
No file size limit, accepted file type, page limit, translation rule or signature rule is published on the AfDB notice, the UNECA notice or the Foundation page. These remain unconfirmed.
official_details.selection_notes: AfDB route: the Bank's Human Resources Department carries out an initial vetting of applications to develop a short list of ten (10) applicant files to be further reviewed by the Foundation; a short list of three (3) candidates is presented to the President of the Bank or his designate for final selection. Only applicants who fully meet the Bank's requirements and are considered for interview will be contacted, and the President reserves the right to appoint a candidate at a lower level. UNECA route: due to an anticipated high volume of applications only finalists are contacted and no feedback is given to unsuccessful applicants; received applications are acknowledged within one week; an update is posted to the ECA fellowship page once selection concludes. The Mo Ibrahim Foundation page does not publish a selection method of its own beyond routing applicants to the hosts.
application_steps: Choose the host organisation route from the links published on the Mo Ibrahim Foundation fellowships page: African Development Bank (Abidjan), International Trade Centre (Geneva) or UNECA (Addis Ababa).

AfDB route: go to the vacancy page for the 2027 Mo Ibrahim Foundation Leadership Fellowship Program and complete the online application form on the Bank's recruitment system (external candidates apply at https://afdb.jobs2web.com/job-invite/2343/).
AfDB route: prepare a comprehensive CV that states date of birth, nationality, education and relevant experience, and attach copies of academic transcripts and three letters of recommendation.

UNECA route: create an account on the UN Inspira system (https://inspira.un.org), then build a draft Administrative Profile with no linked Job Opening and generate it as a PDF; the cover/motivation letter is created as part of that process and appears on page 1.
UNECA route: complete the required online survey and take a screenshot showing the responses were sent, in PDF format.
UNECA route: obtain three letters of recommendation addressed to the '2027 ECA Mo Ibrahim Leadership Fellow Selection Committee'; referees send them to the applicant, not to ECA.

UNECA route: email all documents in one message as PDF attachments to RecruitmentPPost@un.org with the subject line 'ECA 2027 Mo Ibrahim Leadership Fellowship (Applicant Last Name, First Name)'; the AP PDF, degree certificate copies, the three recommendation letters and the survey screenshot must all be in that single email.
ITC route: apply through the ITC vacancy published on the UN Careers system.
Submit before the closing date on the host's own timeline; AfDB closes 20 November 2026 and UNECA closes 20 November 2026 at 11:59 p.m. Addis Ababa time.
Save the submission confirmation. Received applications will be acknowledged within one week on the UNECA route.
applicant_submission_route: The applicant submits the application directly. There is no nomination by a university, ministry or employer on any of the three routes.
AfDB route: online application form on the Bank's website, submitted through the Bank's own recruitment portal (https://afdb.jobs2web.com/job-invite/2343/ for external candidates).
UNECA route: email submission to RecruitmentPPost@un.org. The notice is explicit that the applicant, not the referee and not the institution, sends the complete package.
ITC route: application through the ITC vacancy published on the UN Careers system (https://careers.un.org/jobSearchDescription/285022?language=en).

UNECA route: no portal — applications are emailed to RecruitmentPPost@un.org, with the Administrative Profile PDF generated from https://inspira.un.org. The Foundation page states the 2027 application process is open and directs applicants to each host's website for details and to apply; no Foundation-level closing date is published on the page itself.
The cycle is annual: three Fellows are placed each year.

Regular Bank staff apply through the Bank's internal system; external candidates apply through https://afdb.jobs2web.com/job-invite/2343/.

ITC route: apply through the ITC vacancy published on the UN Careers system at https://careers.un.org/jobSearchDescription/285022?language=en.

official_details.region: Africa-wide eligibility; host institutions in Abidjan (Côte d'Ivoire), Addis Ababa (Ethiopia) and Geneva (Switzerland)

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you are a national of an African country and, for the AfDB route, of an AfDB member country
Count your relevant work experience against the seven-year minimum before starting
Check your age against the 40 / 45-with-children limit
Identify which host organisation you are applying to and read that host's own page, because the application system and possibly the closing date differ
Register on the host's recruitment system early and confirm the account email works
common_rejection_risks: Fewer than seven years of demonstrably relevant work experience
Applying through the wrong host system or missing the host-specific cut-off while meeting the Foundation date
Missing the three letters of recommendation - the AfDB notice states applications are only considered if these are attached
Ineligible profile: government officials, active military personnel, political party leaders, current or former Bank staff, or close relatives of Bank staff
CV that omits date of birth, nationality, education or relevant experience, all of which the AfDB notice requires
CV that reads as generalist rather than showing the private-sector experience and development-policy analysis the AfDB notice prioritises
estimated_uncovered_costs: Living costs beyond the stipend: the published pages do not state that the stipend fully covers housing or living expenses
Your own medical insurance, child education and retirement plan arrangements - for the AfDB route the Foundation arranges that you have them but does not publish that it pays for them
Visa and residence costs, if any are not covered by the mission travel provision
document_audit: CV: include date of birth, nationality, education and relevant experience in one document
Academic transcripts: attach copies for each degree cited
Letters of recommendation: three, and confirm each referee submits or supplies them in the format the host system accepts
Check the file format and size limits of the host's portal before uploading; re-save scans at a readable resolution

alerts.trigger: Host-system cut-off could fall before the Foundation's published 20 November 2026 date
alerts.message: Apply through the host organisation's own page and treat that page's closing date as binding.
If you are not ready by late September, the next opportunity is the following year's cycle, not a rolling intake.

submission_workflow: Choose the host organisation
Read the host's own vacancy or programme page end to end

referee_tracking.instructions: The published notice requires applicants to attach three letters of recommendation. Track each referee individually and confirm the attachment appears on your submitted application, since the notice states applications are only considered if they are attached.

post_award_requirements: Sign a contract with the host institution before commencing service
Comply with the host's Staff Regulations and Rules for operational and conduct purposes
For the AfDB route, the Fellow is barred from applying for a Bank staff post for one year after the Fellowship ends
Arrange personal medical insurance, child education and retirement plan cover as the Foundation requires you to hold
important_advice_for_students: This is a job, not a scholarship. Budget your relocation to Abidjan, Addis Ababa or Geneva on the assumption that the $100,000 stipend is the only guaranteed income: no official page states that it covers housing, meals or day-to-day living costs, and no housing allowance is published.

You must fund your own medical insurance, your children's education and your retirement plan for the whole 12 months. On the UNECA route the notice states this in terms; on the AfDB route the Foundation only ensures that you have these arrangements, it does not pay for them.
Apply on the host page you actually want, and treat that host's deadline as binding. The three routes are three different systems with three different forms and document lists.

On the UNECA route, letters of recommendation must come to you, not to ECA. A letter the referee emails directly to ECA is not counted, and a submission with fewer than three letters is treated as incomplete and not reviewed.
On the UNECA route, submit everything in one email as PDFs. Splitting the package across emails is explicitly not accepted, and where several emails arrive only the last is read.

Do not send undergraduate transcripts or high school documents on the UNECA route. The notice says they are not required and that baccalaureate-level documentation is unnecessary because a master's is the minimum.

Budget extra time for the Inspira Administrative Profile. ECA cannot pull a draft AP from Inspira, so if the PDF is not attached your application is never opened. Contact kassahunb@un.org for technical support well before the deadline.
There is no feedback if you are unsuccessful. Only finalists are contacted.

Do not assume a Fellowship leads to a job at the host. On the AfDB route you are barred from applying for a Bank staff post for a year after the Fellowship, and there is no presumption of future employment.
All three hosts place their emphasis on private-sector experience and development-policy analysis. A CV that is purely academic or purely governmental reads as a weaker fit than the notice asks for.
questions_to_ask_host: What is the exact closing date and time on this specific host's system, and does it differ from the 20 November 2026 date the Foundation publishes?
What file formats and maximum file sizes does the host's portal accept for the CV, transcripts and recommendation letters?
Is there a stated page limit or word limit for the CV, and must the CV follow a host template?
Does the host require the three recommendation letters to be on letterhead, signed, or in any specific language?
What are the net-of-tax implications of the monthly stipend in the host country, and does the host deduct anything at source?
Where is the Fellow expected to live, is accommodation arranged or subsidised in any way, and what are typical local living costs against the stipend?
Does the host provide any supplementary health cover beyond the Fellow's own policy, and what does staff medical insurance cost locally?
What are the host's rules on the Fellow's dependants accompanying them, and on schooling for children?
Who pays for a return visit home during the 12 months, and what happens if the Fellowship ends early?
What is the exact reporting line and the expected weekly time commitment, given that the Fellow complies with the host's Staff Regulations and Rules?
Does the host provide a completion certificate or reference at the end of the 12 months?

records.region: South Africa (study must be in South Africa) - for citizens of any African country
records.duration: Maximum two years of funding; one year for an Honours degree, one or two years for a Masters
records.deadline: Applications for 2028 will open 9 March 2027. Applications close by the end of Wednesday, 14 April 2027 23:59 GMT+2.
records.application_period: The applications timeline runs from March to November of each year for the following year's intake. For the Class of 2028: applications open Tuesday 9 March 2027 and close 14 April 2027 23:59 GMT+2.
records.description: The Mandela Rhodes Scholarship funds a one-year Honours degree or a two-year Masters degree in any field at a recognised South African institution of higher education, and pairs it with a compulsory Leadership Development Programme of residential workshops and regional pods. The Foundation states it offers comprehensive funding for the core costs of study: tuition and registration fees, a study materials allowance, research and conferencing grants on request, a medical aid allowance, accommodation and meal allowances, a personal allowance, and economy-class flights between the scholar's home country and their South African institution at the start and end of the degree. The Foundation does not pay university application fees, SAQA accreditation of existing degrees, or visa application costs. Specific allowance amounts are set by the Foundation and no figures are published.

records.selection_notes: The Foundation looks for young leaders who aspire to leadership, reconciliation, education and entrepreneurship, and who demonstrate the combination of intellect and character. Applicants are screened in rounds: a notification by mid-July indicates whether the applicant reached Round Two, by end of July for Round Three, and by end of August whether they are invited to a Final Round interview. Final Round interviews are conducted in South Africa in October, and final-round applicants based outside South Africa are flown in for an in-person interview with the selection committee. Selected scholars are notified by the end of October.
records.notes: The scholarship cannot be deferred: you must accept it for the year it is offered. Attendance at the residential workshops and regional pods is mandatory and a condition of the scholarship, and the Foundation will not accept travel outside South Africa, even for research purposes, as a reason for absence. You may not hold other scholarships or funded opportunities and may not do paid work for more than 12 hours a week. The award is conditional on you being offered a place at a South African institution, and the Foundation does not apply to universities for you. If you are not accepted by a South African institution in time, you cannot accept the scholarship. The Foundation does not pay visa application costs, and states that a delayed visa may mean you cannot start on time and could lose the scholarship. Applicants from outside South Africa may need SAQA verification, which the Foundation states can take 4-8 weeks and is not covered by the award. Any amount you owe prior to becoming a Scholar is your sole responsibility. The Foundation does not fund MBAs, block courses, or courses delivered predominantly online, and distance learning is not allowed.

official_details.citizenship_residency: Citizens of an African country, no matter where they are currently living or studying. Study must be in South Africa, at a South African institution of higher education; study in the applicant's home country and distance learning are not allowed.
purpose: Combine financial support with a compulsory leadership development programme that 'will challenge you, grow you, and connect you to young African changemakers' (Explore & apply page).

Equip young African leaders with the competence and courage to transform the continent into a place where everyone has equal opportunity to thrive, keeping Nelson Mandela's legacy alive (Explore & apply page).

Build a pipeline of ethical African leaders by selecting scholars who aspire to leadership, reconciliation, education and entrepreneurship and who demonstrate the potential to live them out (How are Mandela Rhodes Scholars selected).

The programme is built on the Foundation's founding principles of reconciliation, education, entrepreneurship and leadership, and on 'a belief that leadership begins with inner transformation' (Explore & apply page).

Produce scholars who use their talents to advance equality, freedom and human dignity in Africa, and who reflect deeply on their own leadership and undergo a process of personal change and growth (eligibility character statements).
sdg_requirement_details: No SDG, development goal or impact-reporting requirement is published. The Foundation publishes four founding principles (reconciliation, education, entrepreneurship, leadership) and states that its programme is delivered through workshops, regional pods and an optional Mentoring Programme, but it does not frame any part of the scholarship against the UN Sustainable Development Goals or Agenda 2063.

The Foundation does ask scholars, after the scholarship, to reply to written requests for updates of personal details so that the MRF can report on its impact — but this is an alumni reporting duty, not an SDG alignment requirement.
study_type: Postgraduate degree study: a one-year Honours degree or a one-to-two-year Master's degree, or their academic equivalents
Full-time study only; distance learning is not allowed
Paired with a compulsory Leadership Development Programme of residential workshops and regional pods, with in-person and online gatherings
official_details.degree_award: A full accredited postgraduate degree, not a short-term award. The Scholarship funds a one-year Honours degree or an up-to-two-year Master's degree (or academic equivalents) at a South African-located tertiary institution registered with the South African Council of Higher Education and approved by the MRF. The degree itself is awarded by the university, not by the Foundation.
official_details.tuition_rule: The MRF pays tuition and registration fees as set by the Scholar's university or institution, and pays them directly to the tertiary institution rather than to the Scholar (Explore & apply FAQ 'How do the finances work'; Terms and Conditions clause 3). Payment is conditional: allowances and fees are released twice a year against proof of registration and a progress report from the institution no later than two weeks after the start of the second semester. If a Scholar receives a rebate from the institution, the MRF will not refund the amount of the rebate (Terms and Conditions clause 4). A Scholar who fails to comply with the requirements for continued study in the registered course loses MRF financial support (clause 7).
official_details.home_tuition_rule: Not applicable as a funding rule: the Scholarship cannot be used to study in the applicant's home country. The Foundation states that the scholarship is for study in South Africa, at a South African institution of higher education, and that distance learning is not allowed, because the Scholar must be at a South African institution in order to participate in the Leadership Development Programme.
official_details.host_institution_fee: Tuition and registration fees are paid by the MRF directly to the tertiary institution, as set by that institution. University application fees are not paid by the MRF. A Scholar may not change their institution of study from the one indicated on their application unless in exceptional circumstances explicitly approved by the MRF (Terms and Conditions clause 5).

masters: Masters students receive one or two years of funding; the overall tenure is capped at a strict maximum of two years with no exceptions allowed.

Many South African Masters degrees require a completed four-year programme or an Honours degree. The Foundation advises checking the exact requirements with the intended department and university, as they may require SAQA verification of qualifications, which can delay both university acceptance and the visa.
Masters programmes in South Africa may require several years of work or clinical experience as an admission requirement; it is the applicant's responsibility to check and to apply for backup options.

host_requirements: The Scholar must study at a South African-located tertiary institution registered with the South African Council of Higher Education, and approved by the MRF, for an accredited postgraduate degree programme (Terms and Conditions clause 1).

The Foundation publishes a list of institutions where a Scholar can study, including AFDA, Cape Peninsula University of Technology, Durban University of Technology, Mangosuthu University of Technology, Monash University South Africa, Nelson Mandela Metropolitan University, North West University, Rhodes University, Tshwane University of Technology, University of Cape Town, University of Fort Hare, University of Free State, University of Johannesburg, University of KwaZulu-Natal, University of Limpopo, University of Mpumalanga, University of Pretoria, University of Stellenbosch, University of the Free State, University of the Western Cape, University of the Witwatersrand, University of Venda, University of Zululand, Vaal University of Technology and Walter Sisulu University.

The award is conditional on the Scholar being offered a place at the relevant institution. The MRF does not apply to universities on the applicant's behalf; the applicant must apply separately, and is advised to apply to several universities and to apply early.
A Scholar may not change their institution of study from the one indicated on the application unless in exceptional circumstances explicitly approved by the MRF.
Scholars must be able to do written and verbal academic work in English at a postgraduate level, as English is the main medium of tuition at South African universities.

Applicants from outside South Africa may need to complete SAQA verification before starting at a South African university. Applying for SAQA verification is not required in order to apply to the Scholarship, but the Foundation advises doing it as soon as possible if you reach the second and third rounds.
document_format_rules: Three letters of recommendation are required and must be in English. Recommenders submit their letters themselves through the application platform; the application cannot be submitted without them and will not be considered without them.
Once a recommender is registered on the platform they receive an email asking them to log on and upload their letter.
Certificates of completion for degrees, transcripts of academic results, and scans of ID and passport documents must be uploaded. Your documents and transcripts must be provided in English.
Two short essays are required: one on your personal journey, and one on a specific question relating to the Foundation's principles.
You must fill in your proposed course of study on the application. The Foundation does not require proof that you have applied to a university.
SAQA verification can take 4-8 weeks and can delay university acceptance and the study visa.

No file size limit, accepted file type, page limit, signature rule or document-expiry rule is published on the pages read for any document. The Foundation's own English-language self-test is offered as a link from the eligibility checker, but no required IELTS or TOEFL score is published.
official_details.selection_notes: Screening proceeds in rounds against the published timeline: applicants are notified by mid-July whether or not they are through to Round Two; by the end of July whether or not they are through to Round Three; by the end of August whether they are invited to a Final Round interview or have been unsuccessful. Final Round interviews are conducted in South Africa in October, and final-round applicants based outside South Africa will be flown in for an in-person interview with the selection committee. Selected scholars are notified by the end of October. After selection, Scholars must do their best to secure acceptance at their university of choice and their study visa for travel to South Africa in January.

Add three recommenders on the platform as soon as it opens. Each registered recommender receives an email asking them to log on and upload their letter.
Contact the three people who will write your recommendation letters before applications open, to ask permission and give them time to write and upload their letters.
Upload certificates of completion for your degrees.
Upload transcripts of your academic results, in English.
Upload scans of your ID and passport documents.
Write and upload two short essays: one on your personal journey, and one on a specific question relating to the Foundation's principles.
State your proposed course of study on the application. Proof that you have applied to a university is not required.
Have your three recommenders sign in to the platform and upload their English letters.

Applications close by the end of Wednesday 14 April 2027 23:59 GMT+2. No late or incomplete applications will be accepted under any circumstances, and your application cannot be submitted without the letters.
Apply separately to your South African university as soon as you can, and to more than one university, because the award is conditional on being offered a place.
applicant_submission_route: The applicant submits their own application online. There is no nomination, university submission or institutional intermediary: the Foundation states 'You must apply online. You can log onto our applications platform to access your application and upload your documents and essays.'
The three referees submit their own letters directly on the same platform once registered by the applicant; the applicant does not upload them on their behalf.
The applicant applies separately and directly to the South African university for the degree; the Foundation states it does not apply to universities on the applicant's behalf.
official_details.application_portal: The Mandela Rhodes Foundation applications platform, accessed through https://www.mandelarhodes.org/scholarship/apply/. The Foundation does not publish a direct platform URL; it states that applicants access the platform through its website.
arrival_rules: Scholars must travel to South Africa in January to take up the Scholarship: 'Selected Mandela Rhodes Scholars must do their best to secure acceptance at their university of choice, and their study visa for travel to South Africa in January.'
You need a visa in order to take up the scholarship in South Africa. The MRF does not support or pay for the visa process.

If your visa is delayed you may not be able to start your academic programme and the Leadership Development Programme on time, and this could result in you losing the scholarship. Apply for your visa as soon as you have received acceptance from your university of choice.

If you are not accepted to a South African university in time you will not be able to get your study visa in time for the commencement of the programme in January, and you will not be able to accept the Scholarship.
Scholars must secure admission to their university of choice by January of their year in residence.

Applicants from outside South Africa may need to complete SAQA verification before they can start at a South African university; the Foundation states this can take 4-8 weeks and can delay university acceptance and the visa.
Economy-class flights are covered for international Scholars only, from the Scholar's home to their institution at the beginning and end of their degree.
timeline_rules: The applications timeline runs from March to November of each year, for the following year's intake.
March: applications open on Tuesday 9 March 2027; candidates can add recommenders and begin uploading documentation and working on their essays.

April: applications close by the end of Wednesday 14 April 2027 23:59 GMT+2, by which time all documentation must be uploaded and the recommenders must have uploaded their references for the application to be complete. No late or incomplete applications will be accepted under any circumstances.
July: notification by mid-July on Round Two; by the end of July on Round Three.
August: notification by the end of August of a Final Round interview invitation or of unsuccess.

October: Final Round interviews are conducted in South Africa in October, with final-round applicants based outside South Africa flown in for an in-person interview. Selected scholars are notified by the end of October.
October to December: selected Scholars must secure university acceptance and their study visa for travel to South Africa in January.
Allowances are paid twice a year, conditional on proof of registration or acceptance and receipt of the institution's progress report no later than two weeks after the start of the second semester.

official_application_route: Apply online on the Mandela Rhodes Foundation applications platform, accessed through https://www.mandelarhodes.org/scholarship/apply/ when applications open on 9 March 2027.

The applicant's three referees submit their own English letters on the same platform after the applicant registers them; without the letters the application cannot be submitted and will not be considered.

The applicant applies separately and directly to one or more South African tertiary institutions for admission; the award is conditional on being offered a place and the Foundation does not apply on the applicant's behalf.

Applicants who reach the second and third rounds are advised to apply for SAQA verification of their qualifications as soon as possible; SAQA verification is not required in order to apply for the Scholarship and the MRF does not cover its cost.
official_details.program_type: Foundation postgraduate scholarship with a compulsory leadership development programme
official_details.region: South Africa (study must be at a South African institution); open to citizens of any African country

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you are an African citizen aged 19 to 29 in the year you apply and under 30 when you take up the scholarship
Check your undergraduate marks are above 70% or an upper second, and that the degree is completed by 1 January 2028
Register on the Foundation's applications platform from 9 March 2027 and add your three recommenders early
Ask three people who know you well and have insight into your character to write English reference letters, ideally before applications open
Start SAQA verification early if you are applying from outside South Africa, as the Foundation states it can take 4-8 weeks
Begin university applications to more than one South African institution in parallel, because the award is conditional on admission
Read the Foundation's full terms and conditions PDF linked from the apply page before you commit
common_rejection_risks: Incomplete application: it cannot be submitted without the three referees uploading their letters, and late or incomplete applications are not accepted under any circumstances
Missing the 14 April 2027 23:59 GMT+2 cut-off, which is absolute
Academic results below 70% or below an upper second
Age outside the 19 to 29 band in the year of applying, or 30 or older at the point of taking up the scholarship
Choosing an MBA, a block course, a course delivered predominantly online, or distance learning, none of which are funded
Failure to obtain admission to a South African institution in time, which makes the award unusable regardless of selection
Degree not completed by 1 January 2028 for the Class of 2028
Weak or generic essays: one is on your personal journey and one answers a question tied to the Foundation's principles
estimated_uncovered_costs: University application fees, which the Foundation states it does not pay
SAQA accreditation of existing qualifications, which may be an entry requirement to your course and is not covered
Visa application costs, which the Foundation states are your responsibility
Passport or other travel document costs, which the Foundation states it does not cover even for shortlisted candidates flying in for an interview
Interim flights, transfers or family visits, since only economy-class flights to and from South Africa at the start and end of the degree are listed
Any debt or amount owed by you before becoming a Scholar
document_audit: Letters of recommendation: three, written in English, uploaded by the referees themselves on the platform, not emailed to you
Transcripts and documents must be provided in English
Upload readable scans of degree certificates, ID and passport; check the platform's file type and size limits before uploading
Have your passport ready early: it is a required upload and visa timing depends on it
Do not wait for a university's offer before submitting; the Foundation states proof of having applied is not required, only the stated course of study

alerts.message: Register that day; referee letters take time and the application cannot be submitted without them.

alerts.trigger: Round notifications from mid-July to end of August 2027
alerts.message: Plan for the Final Round interview in South Africa in October 2027 if you are shortlisted, including the cost and time of travel if you live outside South Africa.
Secure university admission and apply for your South African study visa as soon as you are selected; a delayed visa can cost you the scholarship.
The award cannot be deferred to a later year, so decide before you accept.

submission_workflow: From 9 March 2027, register on the applications platform
Add your three recommenders and send them the platform's notification email details
Draft the personal journey essay
Draft the essay answering the published question relating to the Foundation's principles
Upload degree completion certificates
Upload academic transcripts in English
Upload scans of your ID and passport
Enter your proposed course of study
Track each referee and confirm their letters appear on your application
Submit before 14 April 2027 23:59 GMT+2 and save the confirmation

referee_tracking.role: Letter of recommendation (three required, in English)
referee_tracking.instructions: The referees must sign in to the Foundation's application platform and upload their letters directly. Once you register a recommender they receive an email asking them to log on and upload. Approach three people with relevant experience of you and insight into your character well before applications open, and track each one individually: the application cannot be submitted without all three.

post_award_requirements: Attend all residential workshops and regional pods; there are three workshops in year one and two in year two for a two-year programme
Complete feedback forms and reflections timeously as a requirement of the award
Submit proof of registration at the start of the year
Submit a progress report from your university two weeks after the start of the second semester
Do not hold other scholarships or funded opportunities, and keep paid work to no more than 12 hours a week
Provide updates and details after the scholarship so the Foundation can report on impact
important_advice_for_students: Line up your three referees before applications open on 9 March 2027. The application cannot be submitted without their letters, they upload them themselves, and the whole thing closes at 23:59 GMT+2 on 14 April 2027.
Give referees a deadline with real margin, not the 14 April date. A missing letter is an automatic non-submission, not a late submission you can appeal.
All your documents and transcripts must be in English. If they are not, arrange certified English translation before you upload.
Apply to universities now, in parallel with the scholarship application, and apply to more than one. The award is conditional on being offered a place, and the Foundation will not apply for you.

Start SAQA verification early if you are outside South Africa and your course requires it. It takes 4-8 weeks and can delay both your university acceptance and your visa, and the MRF does not pay for it.
Apply for your study visa the moment you have university acceptance. A delayed visa means you cannot start on time and the Foundation says this could mean losing the scholarship.

Do not budget on the Scholarship to cover your visa, your university application fees, your passport, or SAQA verification. None of these are paid, and the MRF takes no responsibility for injury, sickness, accident or death, so insure yourself.
You cannot defer. If you are offered the Scholarship for a year you cannot start, you must decide then, so check your own readiness before you invest in the application.

The Leadership Development Programme is compulsory, not optional. Three residential workshops in year one and two in year two, some falling at weekends. If your employer or your own commitments make that impossible, this is the wrong award.
You may not hold other scholarships or funded opportunities while you hold this one, and you may not work more than 12 paid hours a week.
No monetary figure is published for any allowance. Do not build a budget on an assumed monthly amount; ask the Foundation directly if you need a number to decide.
questions_to_ask_host: What file formats and maximum file sizes does the Foundation's platform accept for transcripts, certificates, ID and passport scans?
Is there a word limit or page limit for the two essays, and are the essay questions published before you register?
What are the current monetary amounts of the study materials, accommodation and meal, medical aid and personal allowances? None are published on the site.
What is the total annual value of the allowance package, and how does it compare with the actual cost of living and fees at the universities on the published list?
Does the accommodation and meal allowance cover the full cost of university residence, or is a top-up expected?
Is the research and conferencing grant applied for separately, and what is the decision process and cap?
Which universities on the published list will accept my specific qualification without SAQA verification, and which will not?
What exact SAQA documentation do I need, and how long does verification currently take in practice?
Are the workshop dates for the year in residence published, and can they conflict with my academic timetable or a job I still hold?
What happens to my funding if my university acceptance or my visa is delayed past January?
Does the Foundation cover the cost of the October Final Round interview trip for final-round applicants, or is that separate from the stated economy-class degree travel?
Which donors, if any, underwrite my specific Scholarship and what interaction would that involve?

verification.source_conflict_rule: The Explore & apply page governs the published funding scope, the not-covered list, the application process and the timeline. The Terms and Conditions PDF governs tenure conditions, financial mechanics, rebates, institutional changes, donor interaction, failure to meet degree requirements, personal-update obligations and liability. Where the two differ, the Terms and Conditions are treated as binding, because they are the Foundation's contractual document.
verification.source_freshness_rule: The cohort and its dates change every year, so a stale page carries last cycle's opening date and must be re-verified before use. The list of participating institutions and the award conditions are also reviewed between cycles; the Terms and Conditions are the version that is applied to a Scholar when the award is taken up.

records.deadline: Every year, the application portal for our flagship TEF Entrepreneurship Programme opens on the 1st of January till midnight on the 1st of March at Midnight, on our digital platform, www.TEFConnect.com.

records.description: The TEF Entrepreneurship Programme is the Tony Elumelu Foundation's flagship annual programme for African entrepreneurs, combining business management training, mentorship, coaching and a USD 5,000 non-refundable seed capital award. The application is completed on the TEFConnect digital platform and the business assessment test score determines eligibility. Selected participants complete training modules on TEFConnect, submit a business plan, financial projection and pitch video, and then provide business registration, tax and banking documents before the seed capital is paid into their business account. This is a business grant and training programme, not a scholarship, so no tuition or living costs are paid.

records.selection_notes: Independent third-party experts review eligible applications. A minimum score in the business assessment test is required or the applicant is notified as ineligible and encouraged to reapply the following year. Eligible applicants undergo LSEG World-Check global compliance screening and a physical verification exercise by authorised enumerators, which may be in person or virtual. Shortlisting is evaluated on business feasibility, market opportunity, financial understanding, scalability, and leadership and entrepreneurial skills. In the investment readiness phase an independent audit consulting firm reviews the business plan, financial projection and pitch video and ranks participants for investment readiness. Shortlisted participants are notified of participation on the 22nd of March each year.
records.notes: The seed capital is non-refundable and is not a scholarship: it does not pay tuition or living costs, and applicants must fund their own living expenses throughout the cycle. The portal is only open for two months a year, 1 January to midnight 1 March; there is no rolling intake, so missing the window means waiting a full year. You cannot have previously benefited from any TEF programme, and you cannot reapply within the same application window of the same year, which the Foundation states explicitly. Programme participants whose documents are found inauthentic, contain discrepancies, or match the document details of past TEF Entrepreneurship Programme beneficiaries are immediately disqualified. Seed capital payment requires signing the seed capital undertaking and is processed into the business account you provide.

selection_criteria: Business feasibility: the viability of the business idea in its current environment, including practicality, sustainability and associated risks, with a clear value proposition, a well-defined business model and the ability to address an existing problem or need

Market opportunity: a well-defined target market with substantial demand, assessed on size, accessibility and growth potential, plus how the business differentiates itself from competitors, with market research insights and a clear customer-acquisition strategy

Financial understanding: a strong grasp of financial management and the ability to make informed financial decisions, covering cost structures, revenue streams, pricing models, profitability projections, resource management and expense tracking
Scalability: whether the business model can be replicated, expanded into new markets or attract investment over time, with capacity to increase revenue while maintaining or improving efficiency
Leadership and entrepreneurial skills: leadership qualities, resilience and a proactive mindset, with demonstrated innovation, problem-solving ability and commitment to long-term success
Minimum score in the mandatory business assessment test: applicants who do not reach it are classified ineligible and are not reviewed further

official_details.citizenship_residency: Africans aged 18 and above who reside in Africa and plan to establish their business in Africa. The Foundation states its programme reaches all 54 African countries and regions.
purpose: Empower African entrepreneurs and entrepreneurship on the continent. The Tony Elumelu Foundation Entrepreneurship Programme is described as 'the largest African philanthropic initiative committed to empowering African entrepreneurs and entrepreneurship on the continent'.
Select and build the most promising African entrepreneurs so that only those with the greatest potential to drive economic growth and create jobs receive training, mentorship and funding.
Provide training on the TEFConnect digital hub and direct funding so entrepreneurs can start, manage and scale their businesses, and so they create direct and indirect jobs.
Onboard beneficiaries into the TEF Alumni network, where graduates are referred to as Tony Elumelu Entrepreneurs, TEF Alumni and/or TEF Beneficiaries, to keep contributing to Africa's transformation.
sdg_requirement_details: No SDG, development-goal or impact-alignment requirement is published in the selection process. The Foundation does not ask applicants to map their business plan to a specific Sustainable Development Goal, and no SDG reference appears in the published eligibility criteria or shortlist criteria.

The Foundation separately runs gender and green programmes (BeGreen Africa, Women Entrepreneurship for Africa) and publishes impact reporting, but these are separate initiatives, not a condition of the flagship Entrepreneurship Programme application.

official_details.selection_notes: The process runs in six phases after application. Applications are immediately and automatically reviewed when the window closes and applicants are notified via TEFConnect and email of their category. Independent third-party experts review applications deemed eligible, assessing the business idea for feasibility, scalability, market potential and financial viability. Shortlisted applicants undergo LSEG World-Check screening, a global risk-intelligence database, to ensure compliance with global financial and business regulations, then a Physical Verification Exercise by authorised enumerators to confirm identity and the legitimacy of the business documents provided, conducted by physical visit or virtually. Only applicants who pass application review, global compliance and physical verification are considered for the cohort. Successful applicants are notified of participation confirmation on 22 March each year. In the investment readiness phase, an independent audit consulting firm reviews the business plan, financial projection and pitch video, indicates areas of improvement, and ranks participants on investment readiness. In the seed capital phase the TEF Audit and Finance team reviews the disbursement documents.
application_steps: The application portal opens on 1 January and closes at midnight on 1 March each year on the TEFConnect digital platform.

Register on TEFConnect and complete the programme's application form with valid and accurate responses, across four sections: personal information; business idea and experience information; business assessment test; declaration.
Complete all mandatory fields in the online application form.

Attach the requested documents: a valid government-issued ID displaying date of birth and photo, and a high-resolution headshot. Ensure the name and personal details on TEFConnect exactly match the government-issued ID.
Submit the form.
Receive a notification on screen and by email confirming eligibility status and next steps.
Applicants classified ineligible may reapply the following year; there is no appeal route in the published process.

If confirmed as a participant, attend the onboarding session, physical or virtual, and then complete 100% of all training modules on TEFConnect, participate in coaching sessions and engage with the assigned mentor.
Submit a business plan, financial projection and a 2-3 minute pitch video using the templates supplied, for independent audit review and investment-readiness ranking.
Open a business account at one of the partner banks the Foundation lists, so fund tracking and disbursement are easier.

Submit the seed capital documents: government-issued ID, Business Registration Certificate, evidence of tax registration in the business name, a bank reference letter, a Partner Consent form if a co-owner, and a medical report from a reputable hospital if living with a disability.
Sign the TEF Entrepreneurship Programme seed capital undertaking so that payment can be processed into the business account.
Receive the acknowledgement form, the Certificate of Completion and Achievement, and onboarding into the TEF Alumni network.
applicant_submission_route: The applicant submits their own application directly. There is no institutional nomination, university submission, referee-mediated submission or intermediary: registration and submission are on the applicant's TEFConnect account.
Physical verification may involve an authorised enumerator visiting the applicant, or being conducted virtually, so the applicant must be reachable at the address and number given on the application.
The seed capital is paid into the business account the participant provides, so the participant must personally control and open that account.
official_details.application_portal: www.TEFConnect.com - the TEFConnect digital platform. The Foundation states the application portal for the flagship programme opens on 1 January and closes at midnight on 1 March on this platform.
timeline_rules: The application window opens on 1 January and closes at midnight on 1 March every year.

Shortlisted participants are invited to an onboarding session, physical or virtual, after which they are referred to as TEF Entrepreneurship Programme Participants.
The Training Phase follows onboarding and requires 100% completion of all modules on TEFConnect before progression.
The Investment Readiness Phase requires submission of the business plan, financial projection and pitch video, followed by independent audit review and ranking.
The Seed Capital Phase follows successful investment-readiness ranking, with document submission, Audit and Finance endorsement, signature of the seed capital undertaking, and disbursement.
No fixed dates are published for the training, investment readiness and seed capital phases; they are cohort-relative and announced at onboarding.

important_advice_for_students: Treat 1 March midnight as a hard stop. The window closes automatically and late applications are not accepted, so build your application to be submitted and confirmed weeks earlier.

Do not apply if you have ever received anything from a previous Tony Elumelu Foundation programme, or if you already applied in the same window this year. Both are stated disqualifiers, and a first-time application that is wrong costs you a full year.

Make your TEFConnect name and personal details character-for-character identical to your government-issued ID. The Foundation states this exact-match requirement and it also has to hold at the seed capital stage, where your bank reference letter, business name and ID must all agree.

The business assessment test is pass/fail. Applicants who miss the minimum score are classed ineligible with no appeal. Practise before you sit it inside the form, and leave time inside the window to retake it.

Take the shortlist criteria seriously rather than writing a generic business plan: feasibility, market opportunity, financial understanding, scalability and leadership are each separately scored, with market research and financial projections explicitly expected.

Prepare the seed capital documents before onboarding, not after. Business registration, tax registration in the business name, a bank reference letter and the co-owner consent form can each take weeks in some jurisdictions, and every one of them gates the $5,000.

Open the business account at one of the Foundation's partner banks. The Foundation says this makes fund tracking and disbursement easier, and the money is paid into that account, not to you personally.
Complete 100% of the training modules. Partial completion does not progress you to seed capital, whatever else you have done.

If you are a co-owner, the Partner Consent form is mandatory. If you live with a disability, get the medical report from a reputable hospital ready. Both are conditional documents that applicants often leave out.

Budget the $5,000 as capital for the business, not as income for yourself. It is non-refundable and there is no published second tranche, so it does not replace a business plan with real unit economics.
Expect physical or virtual verification by an enumerator after the window closes. Keep your phone reachable and your premises accessible, because this sits between you and the shortlist.

records.description: The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program enables highly talented, service-oriented young people to pursue higher education and is delivered through partner universities and non-governmental organisations rather than through a single central application. Financial support includes tuition fees, accommodation, books and other academic materials, mentoring, counselling, leadership development, and a return air ticket to the Scholar's country of origin if necessary, alongside psychosocial and academic support. purpose: The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program is described by the Foundation as 'a global initiative designed to develop the next generation of transformative leaders by enabling highly talented, service-oriented young people to pursue higher education and cultivate their leadership potential'.
Enable young people to attain inclusive and relevant education, transition smoothly into dignified and fulfilling work, and lead transformative lives.
Envision a transformative network of young people and institutions driving inclusive and equitable socio-economic change in Africa.
Forge powerful partnerships with higher education institutions to deliver robust support to individual Scholars, particularly during their academic journeys and transitions into work.
Create viable pathways for all young people, including women and marginalized groups, so they can improve their lives, livelihoods and well-being, by fostering inclusivity in education pathways.
sdg_requirement_details: No SDG, development-goal or impact-alignment requirement is published for applicants. The Foundation's published focus areas are Education and Transitions, Digital, Agriculture, Health, Refugees and Displaced Persons, Disability Inclusion and Pan-African Programs, but none is stated as a condition of application or of the award.

The Foundation publishes a Young Africa Works strategy and a goal of 100,000 young people accessing higher education by 2030, and it reports on impact, but it does not require applicants to align their studies with a named SDG.

official_details.tuition_rule: Tuition fees are within the published financial support, which the Foundation describes as including 'but not limited to, tuition fees'. The Foundation does not operate a central application or a central waiver: the programme is implemented through partner universities and NGOs, each of which manages its own admission process, fees and timelines, and each partner institution sets its own admission fees. important_advice_for_students: This is a network, not a single scholarship. There is no Mastercard Foundation application form, no Foundation deadline and no Foundation admissions email. Your real task is choosing the right partner institution and winning that institution's admissions process.

Admission is not funding. The Foundation states plainly that gaining admission to a partner institution does not guarantee selection for the Scholars Program, so treat these as two separate hurdles and prepare for both.
You can apply to as many partner universities as you like, and each is a separate application package with a possible separate fee. Decide how many you can genuinely complete well.
If money is the barrier, the admission fee is reimbursable if you are selected. So a partner fee is not a reason to rule out a university — but you should still be ready to fund it up front.

Check the English test requirement before choosing a university. North American universities require TOEFL and/or SAT for international candidates and the Foundation says it cannot influence those requirements. The Foundation's named workaround is choosing an Africa-based partner that does not require SAT or TOEFL.

Do not pay a fee because a Facebook group told you it was a Mastercard Foundation recruitment. The Foundation states it does not solicit funding or request payments from individuals, and it asks you to report such activity to ethics@mastercardfdn.org.
Do not apply for a PhD on the strength of this programme. Scholarships are not currently available to PhD candidates.

You will not get support from the Foundation if you are not awarded a scholarship. The Foundation states it provides no sponsorship or financial support to candidates who are not awarded scholarships through the Programme.

Read what the coverage list does not say. The published support includes tuition, accommodation, books, mentoring, counselling, leadership development and a return air ticket, but the Foundation calls the list non-exhaustive and publishes no itemised budget, no stipend figure and no statement about visa fees, insurance or dependants. Ask the partner in writing what is actually covered.

Start early. Because the deadline is the partner's, and the partner may publish its own earlier internal scholarship deadline for the Mastercard Foundation quota, contact the partner directly about the Scholars Program specifically rather than only about general admission.

verification.source_conflict_rule: The Mastercard Foundation programme page and its FAQ govern what the Foundation itself states: scope, levels, coverage, partner-delivered administration and exclusions. Where the Foundation's programme page and an individual partner institution's guidelines differ, the partner governs its own admissions process, deadline, fees and document requirements, and the partner's page is the one the applicant must follow. Where a partner page and the Foundation's Where to Apply page differ on partner status, the partner's own current listing is treated as current and the discrepancy is recorded rather than resolved in the applicant's favour.
verification.source_freshness_rule: The programme is continuous and the partner network changes during the year, so a partner list read earlier in the year is stale. Any partner institution, deadline or fee older than the current academic cycle must be re-verified directly with the partner, because the Foundation publishes no version date for the institution list and its news items show new partnerships being added during 2025 and 2026.

records.description: The Inlaks Fellowship for Social Engagement is a two-year, non-degree award from the Inlaks Shivdasani Foundation that lets young Indians pursue self-directed work on an issue of public importance under a mentor of their choice. It pays a monthly stipend that varies by cost-of-living category: INR 45,000 in an 'X' category area, INR 35,000 in a 'Y' category area and INR 25,000 in a 'Z' category area, with the final amount at the Foundation's discretion. It supports individual learning only, not organisational work, and fellows must attend three Foundation-hosted workshops at regular intervals.
records.best_fit: Indian citizens residing in India, born on or after 1 January 1991, who hold a bachelor's degree from a recognised Indian institution (or have at least three years of relevant work experience) and want two years to do self-directed research, cause lawyering, grassroots journalism, community-rights, public-health or ecological work.
records.eligibility_summary: Indian citizens residing in India, born on or after 1 January 1991, who are graduates of a recognised Indian institution or have at least three years of relevant work experience, and who are not enrolled in academic study or a PhD for the fellowship period.
eligibility: The applicant must be an Indian citizen currently residing in India.
The applicant must be born on or after 1st January 1991.
The applicant must be a graduate (hold a Bachelor's degree) from a recognised institute/university in India.
In the absence of a Bachelor's degree, they must carry at least three years of relevant work experience.
Those enrolled in academic studies/PhD for the duration of the fellowship are NOT eligible to apply.
Applicants proposing to work on art installations, photo books etc. are not eligible to apply for this fellowship.
coverage: Monthly fellowship stipend for two years, at INR 45,000 / 35,000 / 25,000 per month depending on whether the fellow is living and working in an 'X', 'Y' or 'Z' category area (final amount at the Foundation's discretion)
No tuition, travel, health insurance or equipment costs are listed as covered by the award on the published pages
benefits: Attendance at three workshops hosted by the Foundation at regular intervals during the fellowship
Support to pursue the fellowship project under a mentor of the applicant's own choice
requirements: Complete all questions in the Foundation's Online Application System (OAS)
Enter name, address and latest contact information correctly
For the 'Topic of your project' field, describe the fellowship activity in a few lines so that it correctly represents the nature of the project
Statement of purpose and work plan must be completed in the Foundation's own format and uploaded as PDF only
Your Statement of purpose and work plan must not exceed 1000 words each
The statement of purpose must outline the applicant's personal and professional trajectory very briefly, and the motivation for taking up the project and how it contributes to social change

The work plan must include a title of the proposed work with a concise description of the work or research planned during the fellowship, the expected outcomes, and in detail the manner in which the project will be undertaken with a clear timeline for 2 years
Two letters are required: a Mentor endorsement letter and a Recommendation letter

The Mentor endorsement letter must include a brief description of the mentor's work experience, the mentor's contact details (email and official address), a statement of why the mentor endorses the applicant's work plan, a statement that the mentor agrees to supervise the applicant's work during the fellowship, willingness to review and comment on quarterly and annual progress reports, and willingness to hold periodic meetings with the Foundation so it can assess the fellow's progress

The Letter of Recommendation must elaborate the nature of engagement with the applicant (in what capacity they engaged with the applicant) and the reason why the referee would like to recommend the applicant and the work plan

The Recommendation letter must be from a person who has supervised the applicant's work for at least 6 months; this cannot be the same person as the mentor. For fresh graduates, an academic letter of recommendation is acceptable
The mentor or referee cannot be someone who is currently an Inlaks Fellow or currently being supported by Inlaks under any other opportunity
Please ensure that both the Mentor and Referee letters are also submitted by 15th November 2026, 11:59pm
application_method: Click 'Apply Now' on the fellowship page to reach the Foundation's Online Application System (OAS), hosted on Submittable
Enter personal details; for Date of Birth scroll the calendar or type it exactly as shown on the proof of age and citizenship you upload
Describe the fellowship activity in the 'Topic of your project' field in a few lines
Download the Foundation's statement of purpose and work plan format, complete it and upload it as a PDF
Enter the mentor's email address in the Mentor Endorsement field and submit; the mentor then receives a link by email to upload their Letter of Endorsement
Enter the referee's email address in the recommendation field and submit; the referee then receives a link by email to upload their Letter of Recommendation

Note that the field text may show 'Enter the email address of the person you'd like to serve as a reference' by default even in the Mentor Endorsement section, so the applicant's mentor's email address must be entered there

official_details.description: The Inlaks Fellowship for Social Engagement is a two-year, non-degree award from the Inlaks Shivdasani Foundation that lets young Indians pursue self-directed work on an issue of public importance under a mentor of their choice. It pays a monthly stipend that varies by cost-of-living category: INR 45,000 in an 'X' category area, INR 35,000 in a 'Y' category area and INR 25,000 in a 'Z' category area, with the final amount at the Foundation's discretion. It supports individual learning only, not organisational work, and fellows must attend three Foundation-hosted workshops at regular intervals.

purpose: Give young people the opportunity to build a diverse worldview and establish long-lasting connections to issues of public importance, encouraging them to challenge the status quo while building confidence and security to explore alternatives and make independent choices about their lives.

Create the space that the Indian norm of young graduates joining the workforce immediately does not provide, so that talented individuals can engage with society in a meaningful way and develop critical thinking and a broader view of the world.

Give graduates and early to midcareer professionals the confidence and security to explore alternatives and make independent choices while contributing to social change, and to increase participation in public life among young people.
Enable fellows to learn from a mentor of their choice and to be involved in a process where knowledge drives social change.
The fellowship is committed to supporting equality of opportunity, social inclusion, freedom of expression, and respect for individual and constitutional rights.
sdg_requirement_details: No SDG, development-goal or impact-alignment requirement is published. The Foundation publishes a values commitment — equality of opportunity, social inclusion, freedom of expression, and respect for individual and constitutional rights — and a broad list of acceptable project forms, but does not require applicants to map their project to a named Sustainable Development Goal.

The published project list spans action-oriented research, cause lawyering, grassroots journalism, ecological efforts, community rights, public health, archiving, reviving, and reporting on dying arts, culture and language, so the scheme is issue-agnostic rather than goal-linked.
