host_requirements: Students are matched with a host university or institute according to their area of interest, at top German universities and research institutions, and the intern cannot choose their own provider outside the RISE database.

Host universities, universities of applied sciences (UAS) and institutes provide housing assistance and match students with Ph.D. student mentors or researchers; the mentoring element is stated for UAS only.
The intern's supervisor helps them find reasonably priced housing for the duration of the internship.
The internship must be a project that was submitted to the RISE internship database and is open to general application; personally or institutionally arranged internships are not supported.
Virtual internships are possible only where the individual project description explicitly offers that option, and virtual internships carry different scholarship rates.
German language is not required unless otherwise noted in the individual project description; the working language is English.

The intern may be required to obtain a visa or residence permit and, for some nationalities, must be able to re-enter their home country after the internship. For internships in Germany under the Federal Employment Agency's rules, the intern needs the certificate of enrollment showing an expected graduation date so continuing study in fall 2027 can be confirmed.
document_format_rules: The application process is completely online in the RISE Germany internship database. Applicants must first register for a DAAD ID in order to get access to the database.

Motivation letters: one motivation letter per project applied to. Design and formatting are up to the applicant; DAAD publishes no word or page limit. The salutary address may address the internship provider directly.

Curriculum vitae: should include education, work or volunteer experience, details of interest or previous experience in the field, and may mention involvement in political, cultural and social commitment and special life circumstances. German citizenship holders must add the relevant information about years living outside Germany.

List of courses: a document the applicant writes or produces themselves, no longer than one page, listing courses completed by the time the internship begins. Applicants are told not to copy the entire course catalogue and descriptions.

Transcript: either a digital transcript with university name or logo, student's name and print date, or a copy of a certified hard copy. DAAD states it does not matter if the transcript bears an 'issued to student' stamp.

Certificate of enrollment: some universities do not complete third-party verification forms, in which case DAAD accepts the university's own official enrollment form as long as it shows a prospective, anticipated or expected graduation date. The certificate must show the stamp of the university or college and the signature of an authorized person. DAAD publishes a sample certificate of enrollment for the German Federal Employment Agency at https://www.daad.de/rise/files/2025/11/NEW_CoE_GermanWorkAgency_2025.pdf

The certificate of enrollment is used by the German Federal Employment Agency to decide on approval of the internship, so the expected date of graduation is required to prove ongoing student status. DAAD advises explaining to the Office of Student Services or Registrar that the date is not permanent or binding and is meant to demonstrate current second- or third-year undergraduate status with expected graduation only after the internship.

Letter of reference: must be submitted on the official letterhead of the referee's university and bear the referee's signature. The referee must hold a PhD degree at least. DAAD publishes guidance on what the letter should contain: since when and in what capacity the referee has known the applicant; a ranking statement (among the best 5%, 10%, 20%, 30%, or no assessment possible); how the applicant stands out academically and personally and an assessment of potential; the significance of the scholarship to the applicant's academic and professional career; additional information relevant to the award decision; and a degree of approval (emphatic approval, approval, or conditional approval).

Letter of reference must be uploaded online by the professor. After the applicant logs in and saves the application for the first time, a field named 'Letter of Reference – Please create a link for your professor' appears; entering the professor's name and email creates a web link assigned to that professor, who receives an email and submits the letter online.

The complete required set is described by DAAD as: working PDF documents, transcript, official certificate of enrollment, and a reference letter including an official letterhead and the referee's signature. If anything has not been received online by November 30, 2026, the application cannot be considered.
No file size limit, accepted file-type list beyond the working PDF requirement, translation rule or document-expiry rule is published for the other documents.
official_details.selection_notes: The placement process is formalized because RISE receives a large number of applications from undergraduates and a large number of project offers. First the internship providers send their ranking of applicants. DAAD then ranks undergraduates by academic performance as indicated by GPA, and ranks projects by demand as indicated by the number of applications attracted. The two rankings are matched: the top 30 projects are assigned one of the three applicants they gave highest priority who are still available; the 30 top students by academic performance are assigned one of the three projects they applied for that are still available; and the process continues in this alternating manner until all scholarships are awarded. Once a pair has been matched it is removed from the process. DAAD states the system is not absolute and it always tries to make matches that please both undergraduates and providers, and that it believes the design achieves fairness and transparency. Internship providers are encouraged to contact applicants by phone or email. All providers submit their preference list by the end of January, and DAAD notifies outcomes beginning in March. No individual feedback is provided on an application, by email or by phone.
application_steps: Register for a DAAD ID to gain access to the RISE Germany internship database at https://www.daad.de/rise/en/rise-germany/find-an-internship/application-portal/. The application process is completely online.

Confirm eligibility against the published requirements, including enrolment in a bachelor's programme in the US, Canada, the UK or Ireland, at least two years completed by the time of the placement, and continued undergraduate status afterwards.

Search the internship database. Do not restrict the search to a single field of study, because many projects treat aspects of more than one field and providers must choose a field when submitting offers.
Choose projects carefully and make sure they are in line with your academic field of interest, since withdrawals cause considerable inconvenience for DAAD and the provider.
Read each project description carefully, including whether German is required, whether the project offers a virtual option, and any other project-specific note.
Write one motivation letter per project you apply to, explaining how your past experience has prepared you for the position and optionally your future plans.

Prepare your CV covering education, work or volunteer experience, interest or previous experience in the field, and involvement in political, cultural and social commitment; add special life circumstances if you wish, and for German citizens the information proving six years or more outside Germany.
Produce your own list of courses, no longer than one page, listing the courses you will have completed by the time the internship begins.
Obtain your transcript as either a digital transcript with university name or logo, student's name and print date, or a copy of a certified hard copy.

Obtain an official certificate of enrollment showing a prospective, anticipated or expected graduation date, with the stamp of the university or college and the signature of an authorized person. Use the Office of Student Services or Registrar, and explain that the date is not permanent or binding.
Save your application for the first time so that the 'Letter of Reference – Please create a link for your professor' field appears.

Enter your professor's name and email address in that field. A web link is created and assigned to the professor, who receives an email and submits the letter of reference online, on the official university letterhead, with the referee's signature. The referee must hold a PhD degree at least.
Submit the complete application online by November 30, 2026, 11:59 pm CET. DAAD sends a confirmation email once it receives your complete application.
Ensure the letter of reference reaches DAAD by December 15, 2026, 11:59 pm CET.

Await the placement. Providers submit their preference lists by the end of January, and DAAD notifies applicants of the outcome beginning in March, with positions announced around February/March 2027.
Confirm the start date with your internship provider. Start dates in the offers are meant as a timeframe and are somewhat flexible, determined between you and the provider.
Arrange a European bank account using the IBAN system to receive the monthly stipend and DAAD travel stipends; DAAD recommends an online account and setting it up as soon as you arrive.
Arrange housing with your supervisor's help once you know your city.
applicant_submission_route: The applicant submits directly, online, in the RISE Germany internship database. There is no institutional nomination: RISE Germany 'is a program that offers every applicant the possibility to apply for any internship in the program' and explicitly does not support personal or institutional contacts.
The academic referee submits the letter of reference directly and online, through a link generated by the applicant and emailed to the professor.
The applicant applies to individual internship projects within the database, writing a separate motivation letter for each project applied to.
For Canadian students, a parallel route exists through the Mitacs Globalink Research Internship programme, which offers up to 100 positions for successful matched candidates in RISE Germany.
official_details.application_portal: The RISE Germany internship database at https://www.daad.de/rise/en/rise-germany/find-an-internship/application-portal/, which requires a DAAD ID registration. Canadian students may also apply through the Mitacs Globalink Research Internship programme at https://www.mitacs.ca/en/programs/globalink/rise-globalink-research-internship.
arrival_rules: The internship can start between May 15 and July 15, 2027, for a duration of three months, with a minimum stay of ten weeks and a maximum stay of 90 days.

Start dates in the internship offers are meant as a timeframe and are somewhat flexible; they are determined between the intern and the internship provider, and the FAQ advises getting in touch with the provider if there are questions about dates.
The intern needs a European bank account using the IBAN system to receive the monthly stipend and the travel stipends, and DAAD recommends opening an online account as soon as they arrive in Germany.
Housing is arranged by the intern with the supervisor's help after arrival; no arrival date, arrival grant or relocation support beyond the published international travel subsidy is published.

Visa and residence permit: European citizens do not need a visa; US, Canadian and British citizens staying 90 days or less do not need one either, but students staying longer than 90 days must apply for a visa. Students without those citizenships are strongly advised to check with the German Federal Foreign Office or their embassy.

Enter the academic professor's name and email in the 'Letter of Reference – Please create a link for your professor' field so that a link is generated and the professor can upload the letter online by December 15, 2026.

RISE Germany does not accept applications by post, email or through a home university, and does not support independently arranged internships.

important_advice_for_students: Check your graduation date first. If you finish your degree in spring or summer 2027 you are ineligible for RISE Germany 2027 and must apply to RISE Professional instead. This is German labour law, not a policy choice, and DAAD says it cannot get a work permit waiver for you.

You must still be an undergraduate in fall 2027. The certificate of enrollment has to show an expected graduation date after the internship so the German Federal Employment Agency can be assured of continuing study. When you ask the Registrar for the certificate, say clearly that the date is not permanent or binding and is only meant to prove you are currently in your second or third year.
Do not restrict your database search to one subject. Many projects straddle fields, and because providers must pick a field when they submit an offer, a narrow search makes you miss placements.
You need one motivation letter per project. There is no word or page limit, so write to the project rather than recycling one generic letter.

Get your referee lined up early and check they hold a PhD. The letter must be on official university letterhead with their signature, and must be uploaded online by them, not attached by you. Company referees are not accepted at all.
If your referee is a lab supervisor from a research internship, that internship must have been in a university setting and lasted at least two months, or the letter will not count.
The application deadline and the reference deadline are different: application 30 November 2026, reference 15 December 2026. Missing the first is fatal even if the letter arrives.
Your rank depends on your GPA. DAAD ranks undergraduates in order of grade point average and separately ranks projects by demand. Do not expect the motivation letter to outrank a weak transcript.
Do not withdraw. Withdrawals cause considerable inconvenience for DAAD and the provider, and there is no individual feedback either way.

If you got RISE last year and are still an undergraduate, you can apply again but you must choose a different internship, city or provider, and you cannot apply to RISE Germany and RISE Professional in the same cycle.

Budget the gap yourself. The stipend is stated as help to cover living expenses, housing is not paid by DAAD, and the FAQ specifically warns about rental scams and competitive markets in cities like Munich and Berlin.
Open your IBAN account as soon as you land. You cannot receive the monthly stipend or travel stipends without a European account, and DAAD recommends an online one for speed.

If you stay more than 90 days you need a visa, and if you are not a US, Canadian, British or Irish citizen you may need one even for a short stay. DAAD funds neither the visa nor your flights beyond the stated international travel subsidy.
No feedback is coming. DAAD states it cannot provide individual feedback on your application by email or by phone. Put your energy into the placement process rather than chasing a decision.
questions_to_ask_host: Is German required for this specific project, and if so at what level?
Does this project offer a virtual internship option, and if so what is the scholarship rate for a virtual placement?
How flexible is the start date, and does the three-month period have to be continuous?
What is the weekly time commitment and expected output of the project?
How much housing assistance can the host realistically provide, and what is the typical monthly rent in this city?
What is the name and contact of my supervisor, and do they supervise this project directly?
Does the lab or institute cover research materials and consumables, or do I pay from the stipend?
Who arranges the workplace access, safety induction and any visa sponsorship documentation the Federal Employment Agency requires?
Does the internship count towards my home university's credit requirement, and is there an assessment or report I must produce?
Is the internship paid, unpaid, or does the project offer its own additional funding on top of the DAAD stipend?
What happens if I need an extension or my project runs longer than the agreed period?
Is there funding available for a presentation or publication of the results at a conference?

verification.source_freshness_rule: The cycle is annual and every date in the programme shifts each year, so a page read for one summer is stale for the next. records.description: The Friedrich-Ebert-Stiftung's basic funding programme for international students supports Bachelor's, Master's, Diplom and Staatsexamen degree programmes at German public or state-recognised universities. The published financial support is 992 Euro, with health insurance costs covered and an additional 255 Euro per month for scholarship holders with children. The scholarship does not have to be repaid and is awarded independently of need.

records.selection_notes: The selection procedure has five steps (online application form, documents and expert opinion, first selection interview, second selection interview, decision by the selection committee). From application to decision it can take three to seven months. Applicants who are the first in their family to study and/or have a migration background, as well as women and students at universities of applied sciences and in STEM subjects, are considered in particular.
records.notes: Applications are formally possible both from Germany and from abroad. Good German is required even if the degree programme is taught in English; the foundation states that it accepts level B2 even without a certificate. The FES does not fund second degrees, part-time or dual studies (except where full-time study is evidenced), short-term stays abroad, internships, summer schools, language courses or final-exam-only phases.

award_holder_conditions: The scholarship is not repayable: 'Das Stipendium muss nicht zurückgezahlt werden.'
The scholarship holder must continue to be enrolled in a full-time degree programme at a German public or state-recognised university, higher education institution or university of applied sciences.
The scholarship holder must continue to identify with the fundamental values of social democracy, which the Foundation treats as the basis of the award.
The scholarship holder is expected to remain engaged in civic or socio-political activity, which is one of the three baseline questions an applicant must answer affirmatively.

The scholarship supports the holder ideologically as well as materially: the holder is expected to take up the offer of political education seminars, workshops and skills training, to join local scholarship-holder groups and the 18 thematic working groups, and to be integrated into the network of current and former scholarship holders.
Scholarship holders with children receive an additional monthly amount, which is conditional on the family situation being declared in the application.
The Foundation's published basis for offsetting other income: the Foundation's English page states that any income exceeding 400 Euro per month will be credited against the scholarship.
Travel costs incurred travelling to a selection interview can be reimbursed on submission of the Foundation's form; this is an interview-stage cost, not a study-period cost

Personal Betreuung und Beratung: the Foundation states its funding is characterised by personal supervision and advice for scholarship holders, and that many former scholarship holders act as Mentor:innen on questions around study and career planning
The scholarship may not be used for the excluded purposes listed under not_covered_or_excluded, including a second degree or a language course, unless the holder already holds an FES scholarship

The Foundation is convinced that commitment to society works best when achieved together.
sdg_requirement_details: No SDG, development-goal or impact-alignment requirement is published. The published selection emphasis is on education equity (Bildungsgerechtigkeit), particularly first-generation students, students with a migration background, women, students at universities of applied sciences and STEM students, rather than on any named international goal.

official_details.tuition_rule: The Foundation states that its financial support amounts to 992 Euro per month and that the cost of health insurance is covered, but it publishes no tuition-waiver rule. Where the Foundation's stipend is described, it is described as support for living during the study, not as a fee waiver.
official_details.home_tuition_rule: Not applicable as a published rule. The programme requires the applicant to be already studying at a German institution, and the Foundation explicitly does not fund study abroad programmes outside the EU or short-term stays abroad.

host_requirements: The applicant must already be enrolled at a German public or state-recognised university, higher education institution or university of applied sciences (an einer deutschen, staatlichen oder staatlich anerkannten Hochschule oder Fachhochschule).
Enrolment must be confirmed by an Immatrikulationsbescheinigung, and university entrance qualification and certificates are among the documents requested at the second stage.
The applicant's study must be a full-time degree programme; extra-occupational and part-time courses of study are not funded.
Scholarship holders with children receive an additional monthly amount, which requires a declared family situation.
The Foundation's English page notes particular importance for students at universities of applied sciences, so those institutions are an accepted host type rather than a second-tier route.
document_format_rules: The application is made in the online application form, using the form published for the Grundförderung für Ausländer:innen at https://www.fes.de/oas/portal/pls/portal/bewsti2014.bewmaske?pFprog=2&pkn=A. The online form is required as the first step and is checked by FES staff against the formal and substantive criteria.

The first-step online form requires general personal information, information on professional and family background, the applicant's motivation to become an FES scholarship holder, and information on socio-political engagement.
Applications must be submitted in German.

Second-stage documents requested by email: a detailed CV covering previous education and socio-political engagement; certificates, university entrance qualification, enrolment certificate (Immatrikulationsbescheinigung) and other evidence; a detailed letter of motivation; and two references (Gutachten) from university lecturers, or from teachers for first-year students.

For the Grundförderung, the Foundation publishes a dedicated document and reference checklist as a downloadable file at https://www.fes.de/index.php?eID=dumpFile&t=f&f=160624, which is the governing list of required documents and guidance for this programme specifically.
Applicants have three weeks to assemble the documents and up to six weeks for the references, and the Foundation sends a receipt confirmation on receipt.

If an applicant is invited to a selection interview and has incurred travel costs, those costs can be reimbursed by submitting the Foundation's travel-cost reimbursement form for the Grundförderung (Fahrtkostenerstattung_BMFTR_Grundförderung), published at https://www.fes.de/index.php?eID=dumpFile&t=f&f=165947.
Applicants can log back in at any time before submitting to continue an unfinished online application, and can upload further documents through the same login once they advance a stage.
The Foundation informs every applicant by email about the result of each stage, and the final decision is communicated at the latest one week after the selection committee's meeting.

No file size limit, accepted file-type list, translation rule, certification rule or document-expiry rule is published on the pages read. The documents checklist PDF and the reference-writing guidance are published as separate files and were not downloaded.
official_details.selection_notes: The procedure has five published steps. Step 1: complete the online application form; FES staff check it against formal and substantive criteria, and within two to four weeks of receipt the applicant receives either a rejection or a request to submit documents and references. Step 2: submit documents and references; the file is reviewed and the applicant receives either a rejection or notification that the application has been passed to a Vertrauensdozentin or Vertrauensdozent. Step 3: the first selection interview, a subject-related discussion with a Vertrauensdozentin or Vertrauensdozent, from which a Gutachten is produced and attached to the file; the applicant then receives either a rejection or notification that the file has gone to a member of the selection committee. Step 4: the second selection interview with a person from the selection committee, producing a further Gutachten attached to the file and tabled at the committee's meeting. Step 5: decision by the selection committee, which meets eight to ten times a year; once both Gutachten are available the application is presented in detail to the committee at the relevant meeting and the members decide on admission to the funding programme. The Foundation informs the applicant of the final decision at the latest one week after the meeting, whether that is an offer or a rejection, and states that the whole process from application to decision can take three to seven months.
application_steps: Apply early. The Foundation states the best time to apply is as early as possible, because it wants scholarship holders to benefit from the scholarship for as long as possible, and the deadlines are listed per programme.

Check your degree-stage window. Master's: before or at the start of the first semester of the Master's programme (winter semester by 30 November, summer semester by 31 May). Bachelor, Diplom, Magister, Staatsexamen: after the first semester and up to three semesters before the end of the standard period of study. Medicine: after the fourth semester or after the Physikum, to the end of the sixth semester.

Complete the online application form for the Grundförderung für Ausländer:innen at https://www.fes.de/oas/portal/pls/portal/bewsti2014.bewmaske?pFprog=2&pkn=A, in German, covering general personal information, professional and family background, your motivation to become an FES scholarship holder, and your socio-political engagement.
Submit the form. FES staff check it against the formal and substantive criteria.
Wait two to four weeks. You will receive either a rejection or an email requesting your documents and references.

If invited, submit within the stated windows: three weeks for the documents and up to six weeks for the references. Documents: a detailed CV covering your previous education and socio-political engagement; certificates, university entrance qualification, enrolment certificate and other evidence; and a detailed letter of motivation. References: two Gutachten from university lecturers.
Consult the Foundation's published Grundförderung document and reference checklist at https://www.fes.de/index.php?eID=dumpFile&t=f&f=160624 for the full required list for this programme.
Use your FES login at https://www.fes.de/oas/portal/pls/portal/bewsti2014.login to upload further documents when you advance to the next stage. FES confirms receipt of the documents.
If the file passes, attend the first selection interview, a subject-related discussion with a Vertrauensdozentin or Vertrauensdozent. A Gutachten is produced and attached to your file.
If you advance, attend the second selection interview with a member of the selection committee. A second Gutachten is produced.
If you have travelled for an interview, submit the Foundation's travel-cost reimbursement form for the Grundförderung to claim reimbursement of your travel costs.

Await the decision. The selection committee meets eight to ten times a year and you will be informed by email at the latest one week after the meeting, whether the outcome is an offer or a rejection. The full process from application to decision can take three to seven months.
applicant_submission_route: The applicant submits directly. The online application form, the documents and the references are all submitted by the applicant to the Foundation, with no institutional nomination and no employer or university acting as an intermediary.
Applications may be submitted formally from Germany or from abroad: 'Bewerbungen sind formell sowohl aus Deutschland als auch aus dem Ausland möglich.'

The two Gutachten must be written by university lecturers, or by teachers for first-year students, and submitted by the applicant with the document package within the stated six-week window. The Foundation publishes guidance on preparing the references separately.
After the first stage, further documents are uploaded by the applicant through the Foundation's own application login.
The Foundation's contact addresses for Auslandsförderung are published for questions, not as a submission channel; submission is through the online system.
official_details.application_portal: The Foundation's online application system at https://www.fes.de/oas/portal/pls/portal/bewsti2014.bewmaske?pFprog=2&pkn=A (the Grundförderung für Ausländer:innen form), with applicant login at https://www.fes.de/oas/portal/pls/portal/bewsti2014.login.
arrival_rules: The applicant must already be living in Germany and studying at a German university at the time of application, and applications may formally be submitted from Germany or from abroad. Consequently there is no arrival provision: the applicant is already in Germany when applying.
No arrival date, latest-arrival rule, visa support arrangement or relocation funding is published. Study abroad programmes outside the EU and short-term stays abroad are not funded.
Enrolment must be confirmed by an Immatrikulationsbescheinigung, and the Foundation's stage-two document request includes the enrolment certificate.
timeline_rules: The best time to apply is as early as possible, because the Foundation wants scholarship holders to benefit for as long as possible.

Application windows by degree stage: Master's, before or at the start of the first semester of the Master's programme (winter semester by 30 November, summer semester by 31 May); Bachelor, Diplom, Magister and Staatsexamen, after the first semester and up to three semesters before the end of the standard period of study (English page: until three semesters before finishing the standard period of study, so by the end of the 3rd semester on a six-semester programme or the end of the 4th semester on a seven-semester programme); medicine, after the fourth semester or after the Physikum to the end of the sixth semester. The Foundation's English page also states diploma, magister and state examination by the end of the 6th semester.

There is no single annual closing date: applications are accepted on a rolling basis within the stage-specific windows, which is why the record's deadline_date is only meaningful as the 30 November master's-stage date.
Step 1 to first outcome: within two to four weeks of receiving the online application, the applicant receives either a rejection or a request to submit documents and references.
Step 2: three weeks to assemble the documents and up to six weeks for the references, with a receipt confirmation on arrival.
The selection committee meets eight to ten times a year, and the applicant is informed of the final decision at the latest one week after the meeting.
Total elapsed time from application to decision: three to seven months.
The Foundation informs all applicants by email about the result of each individual stage.
Applicants who have not yet submitted their online application can log in at any time and continue editing it.
official_application_route: Complete the online application form published for the Grundförderung für Ausländer:innen at https://www.fes.de/oas/portal/pls/portal/bewsti2014.bewmaske?pFprog=2&pkn=A, in German.
The form is checked by FES staff against the formal and substantive criteria, and a decision or a document request follows within two to four weeks.

On invitation, submit the document package and two academic references through the Foundation's application login within three weeks for documents and up to six weeks for references, using the Grundförderung checklist at https://www.fes.de/index.php?eID=dumpFile&t=f&f=160624 as the governing list.
Attend the first selection interview with a Vertrauensdozentin or Vertrauensdozent if invited.
Attend the second selection interview with a member of the selection committee if shortlisted.
Submit the Foundation's travel-cost reimbursement form for the Grundförderung if you have incurred interview travel costs.

The decision is communicated by email at the latest one week after the selection committee's meeting. The Foundation does not publish a postal submission route for the Grundförderung; the online system is the route.

important_advice_for_students: You must already be enrolled at a German university when you apply. This is the first gate, and it is not waivable — an offer of admission is not enough, enrolment is. Plan around being in Germany before the window closes.

German is mandatory, not optional. B2 is the level the Foundation states it accepts, and it accepts it without a certificate, but the application must still be written and submitted in German. Even if you study in English, you must prove German.

Check your degree-stage window before anything else. The windows are different for Master's, Bachelor, and medicine, and they are expressed relative to your semester count rather than as a calendar date. Applying in the wrong window is the most likely reason for an automatic rejection.

Check the funding-exclusion list against your course. A two-semester Master's, medical study up to the Physikum, any doctoral or postdoc stage, a research visit, physiotherapy or psychotherapy training, part-time study, and study outside the EU are all excluded. If your programme is short or part-time, this is the wrong scheme.
A second degree or a language course is not funded unless you already hold an FES scholarship. If you are planning to change course, check whether the new course would be a second degree.
Have your first graded performance records in hand before you apply. They are a stated prerequisite, and Bachelor's students must submit them.

Do the two academic references early. You have three weeks for documents but up to six weeks for the references, so the references are the long pole. University lecturers, not teachers, write them unless you are a first-year student.

Write the civic engagement part seriously. Soci-political commitment and identifying with the values of social democracy are two of the three baseline yes/no questions, and the Foundation looks for students who identify with social democracy and treat volunteering as self-evident.

Play to the Foundation's published priority groups if any apply to you: first in your family to study, migration background, women, universities of applied sciences, STEM. The Foundation states it gives particular weight to these applications.

Budget for what is not covered. The published package is 992 Euro per month plus health insurance costs, with an additional amount for children. Tuition and semester fees at your institution are not listed as covered. Ask your university what the semester contribution is and keep it in your own budget.

Watch the offset rule. The Foundation's English page states that any income exceeding 400 Euro per month is credited against the scholarship, so part-time earnings above that threshold reduce your stipend.
Claim interview travel costs if you have them. The Foundation reimburses travel costs for applicants invited to a selection interview, using its own form. Submit it.

Allow three to seven months. The process runs from the online form through a document request, two interviews with two separate Gutachten, and a committee meeting, and the committee only sits eight to ten times a year.

Talk to a scholarship ambassador before you apply. The Foundation points applicants to its stipendien-botschafter:innen for questions and for encouragement before applying, and these are former holders who answer questions they would rather answer themselves.
questions_to_ask_host: What is the current semester contribution fee at my institution, and does the university offer any waiver for scholarship holders? The Foundation does not publish that it pays it.
What health insurance plan will I be enrolled in, and does its cost vary with my age, marital status or dependants? The Foundation says it covers health insurance costs but publishes no figure.
What counts as the 'first graded performance records' required at application, and does my university issue them in a form I can upload directly?
Does my university offer a thesis supervisor or academic mentor willing to write a Gutachten, and how long do they take?
What is the standard period of study for my programme, so that I can calculate the three-semester application window correctly?
Is there a German course requirement attached to my programme that I should start now, given that applications must be submitted in German?
Does my institution have a scholarship-holder network or working group that FES scholarship holders join, and what does it expect of me in terms of time?
How much do the 18 thematic working groups and the political education seminars take in study time, on top of my coursework?
Is my course one of the excluded categories by another name — for example is it run part-time, is it a two-semester Master's, or is it a research stay rather than a degree programme?
What is the Foundation's offset calculation in practice if I have part-time income, and over what period is it assessed?
How do I apply for the additional amount for scholarship holders with children, and what is the current monthly figure?
Can I change my host institution or my subject after being awarded, and does that affect the stipend?

verification.source_conflict_rule: The programme page for Grundförderung für Ausländer:innen governs this specific scheme's scope, package and degree-stage windows, and the online application page governs the procedure, document list and deadlines. The Foundation's English 'Information in English' page is a cross-programme summary covering all FES schemes; where it differs from the programme page, the programme-specific German page governs, and every difference is recorded in institution_check_required rather than silently resolved. Where the English page is the only source for a rule, such as the 400 € income offset, it is cited explicitly as the English page.
verification.source_freshness_rule: The cycle is continuous and the windows are semester-relative rather than calendar-anchored, so there is no single annual date to go stale; what does change is the stipend rate, the family or children's allowance, the fee schedule at German institutions and the exclusion list. All of these must be re-read each academic cycle before an applicant budgets, and the selection committee's eight-to-ten-meetings-per-year cadence means a rejection is not final until a specific meeting date has passed.

data_quality.source_level: Official provider pages (Friedrich-Ebert-Stiftung programme page for the Grundförderung, the Foundation's online application page, and the Foundation's own English-language information page), all on fes.de

records.description: The Konrad-Adenauer-Stiftung's refugee scholarship programme funds Bachelor's, Master's and PhD students who hold a German residence permit. The page is published bilingually in English and Ukrainian. For undergraduate and graduate students the financial support is up to 752 Euro per month depending on income plus 300 Euro for study-related expenses; for PhD candidates it is 1,350 Euro per month plus 100 Euro for research-related expenses. Applications are made online via campus.kas.de.

records.description: The Friedrich-Ebert-Stiftung funds doctoral candidates from abroad who are admitted to doctoral study at a German university. Scholarship holders receive 1,500 Euro per month plus a subsidy for statutory health insurance; funding normally runs for three and a half years and does not have to be repaid. All subjects are funded except medicine. Good German is required, with level B2 accepted even without a certificate.
records.best_fit: International doctoral candidates at a German university who completed their degree with above-average results, whose project makes a significant contribution to research, and who are socially and politically engaged.
records.eligibility_summary: Doctoral candidates from abroad admitted to a German university, with very good German and above-average degree results, whose research project makes a significant contribution to research.

records.selection_notes: The general selection procedure for FES is: online application form, documents and expert opinion, first selection interview, second selection interview, decision by the selection committee. From application to decision it can take three to seven months. Applicants who are first in their family to study and/or have a migration background, as well as women and students at universities of applied sciences and in STEM subjects, are considered in particular.
records.notes: Proof of German is required even when the dissertation is written in English; the foundation accepts level B2 without a certificate. Applicants who have only recently arrived in Germany are explicitly encouraged to describe engagement from their country of origin in the application.

official_details.description: Die Promotionsförderung für Ausländer:innen richtet sich an Promovierende an einer deutschen Hochschule. Voraussetzung für eine Bewerbung sind gute deutsche Sprachkenntnisse. Ein Nachweis über deutsche Sprachkenntnisse ist auch notwendig, wenn die Dissertation in englischer Sprache verfasst wird. Wir akzeptieren ein Sprachniveau von B2, auch ohne Zertifikat. Stipendiat:innen der Promotionsförderung für Ausländer:innen erhalten monatlich 1.500 Euro und einen Zuschuss zur gesetzlichen Krankenversicherung. Die Dauer der Förderung beträgt in der Regel dreieinhalb Jahre; in begründeten Ausnahmefällen länger, maximal jedoch bis zum Zeitpunkt der Abschlussprüfung. Das Stipendium muss nicht zurückgezahlt werden. Der richtige Zeitpunkt für die Bewerbung: bis circa zwei Jahre vor Abgabe der Dissertation.

records.name: Development-Related Postgraduate Courses (EPOS)
records.region: Germany (applicant countries: DAAD/DAC list of developing and newly industrialised countries)
records.duration: 12 to 42 months (dependent on study programme)

records.application_period: Cycle-based: applicants apply directly to a listed EPOS postgraduate course for the published intake year (the current DAAD programme list is headed 'List of Application Deadlines for Intake 2027/2028'); the course's own committee then nominates candidates, who are invited to upload to the DAAD portal for the final selection.
records.description: The DAAD EPOS programme funds individual scholarships for graduates from developing and newly industrialised countries to take a development-oriented postgraduate (mostly Master's) course at a state or state-recognised German university, and in exceptional cases a doctoral degree. The award is a monthly payment of EUR 992 for graduates or EUR 1,300 for doctoral candidates (EUR 1,400 from February 2026), plus payments towards health, accident and personal liability insurance and a flat-rate travel allowance. Under certain circumstances scholarship holders may additionally receive a monthly rent subsidy and a monthly allowance for accompanying family members. Scholarships are awarded subject to funding being provided by the Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ).
records.best_fit: Graduates from DAC-listed developing and newly industrialised countries who hold a Bachelor (normally a four-year course) with above-average results (upper third), have at least two years of professional experience after that degree, and can prove a development-related motivation tied to their work in a public authority or company.
records.eligibility_summary: Graduates with at least two years' professional experience from DAAD-listed developing and newly industrialised countries, who hold a relevant Bachelor degree with far above average results and whose degree is normally not more than six years old.

application_method: Step 1: Send your complete application directly to the postgraduate course you have chosen.
Step 2: A selection committee at the course suggests potential candidates for a DAAD scholarship.

Step 4: The selection process is finalised and the suggested candidates are informed accordingly.
records.selection_notes: Selection is by independent, voluntary selection committees. Candidates must fulfil the academic requirements and be expected to complete the study programme successfully (above-average first academic exam, top performance in the third, language skills), hold a relevant Bachelor degree, have at least two years' professional experience, and prove a development-related motivation. Special circumstances such as a disability may be taken into account.
records.notes: The scholarship call is made subject to the provision of funds by the Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ), so funding is not guaranteed by the DAAD itself. Applications sent to the DAAD are not forwarded and will not be considered - the course must be applied to directly. Applicants resident in Germany for more than 15 months at the application deadline are excluded. Degrees should normally not be more than six years old. Some courses require additional documents. DAAD scholarships do not have to be paid back.

records.name: MOPGA 2027: Visiting Fellowship Program for Early Career Researchers
records.official_source: Campus France, funded by the Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs (MEAE) in partnership with the Ministry of Higher Education, Research and Space (MESRE)
records.region: France (applicants of any nationality except French)
records.duration: 12 months
records.deadline: Application deadline: 15 December 2026
records.application_period: Applications open 15 September 2026 and close 15 December 2026. Results are notified May-June 2027, and successful applicants arrive in France between September and December 2027.
records.description: MOPGA is a French Government visiting fellowship that pays a monthly allowance to early-career foreign researchers to carry out a 12-month research project in a French host laboratory on climate and environmental themes. Each fellowship covers a monthly allowance of EUR 2,500, a EUR 500 settling-in allowance, and health, civil liability and repatriation coverage. Host laboratories receive no funding under the programme; the money is intended solely to cover the invited researcher's living expenses, and international travel costs are not covered.
records.best_fit: Researchers who defended a PhD between December 2021 and December 2026, hold a nationality other than French, are not resident and professionally active in France, and have already lined up a French host laboratory willing to sign a research stay agreement.
records.eligibility_summary: Foreign researchers whose PhD was defended between December 2021 and December 2026 inclusive, applying from outside France for a research stay in France.
eligibility: Hold a doctoral degree awarded less than five years before the application deadline, i.e. have defended your PhD thesis between December 2021 and December 2026 inclusive
Be exclusively of foreign nationality (all nationalities are eligible except French nationality)
Apply for the purpose of undertaking international mobility to France
Not be residing and professionally active in France at the time of application
Not have previously received a MOPGA fellowship
coverage: Monthly allowance of EUR 2,500
EUR 500 settling-in allowance

Health coverage: health insurance, civil liability insurance and repatriation assistance, followed by supplementary health insurance once the fellow has been registered with the French social security system
benefits: Status of French Government Scholarship holder (BGF)
Fellowship paid directly by Campus France
Research stay agreement signed between the French host institution and the researcher
requirements: Applications must be submitted online through the Campus France SMApply platform; applications sent by email will not be considered
A research stay agreement must be signed between the host institution in France and the researcher
Host laboratories undertake to provide an appropriate scientific environment for the research stay, but do not receive any funding under the programme

This French Government fellowship cannot be combined with a French employment contract, such as a research contract or postdoctoral contract, or with any other individual funding awarded by a French government entity
Research project must fall within one of the five MOPGA research areas
application_method: Agree the research project with a host laboratory in France and obtain the host director's commitment

Prepare the research project description: project title, 6 keywords, summary, background and motivation, scientific objectives, methodology and timeline, relevance to MOPGA, and international collaboration or expected impact
Collect the required documents, including supervisor CV and the co-signed support letter
Submit the application online via https://campusfrance.smapply.io/prog/mopga_2027/ before 15 December 2026
records.selection_notes: Selection takes place in two stages: scientific experts appointed by the French Ministry of Higher Education, Research and Space in the relevant fields assess the applications received, then a scientific committee makes the final selection. Innovative approaches involving advanced technologies within the eligible research areas are given particular consideration during the selection process.
records.notes: The fellowship is not renewable and lasts exactly 12 months. International travel costs to France are not covered by the programme; the host laboratory may be able to help but is not funded to do so. The award cannot be combined with a French employment contract (research contract or postdoctoral contract) or any other individual funding from a French government entity. A PhD defended after December 2026 is not eligible. If the doctoral degree certificate has not yet been issued, an official certificate confirming the defence, proof of thesis submission, or another official institutional document is accepted. For researchers who obtained their PhD more than five years ago, the eligibility window may be extended by 18 months per child, or by the actual duration of maternity leave, on submission of supporting documents noted in the application file. Only projects with a genuine integrated 'One Health' approach qualify under the human, animal and environmental health theme; projects focused solely on medicine or human health are not eligible.

records.name: AAPG - Appel à projets générique 2027 (ANR Generic Call for Proposals 2027)
records.region: France (project applicants in the French research system, with international bilateral collaborations via the PRCI instrument)
records.duration: Project duration set by the applicant; grants are awarded annually across the project period
records.deadline: Clôture du dépôt et enregistrement Etape I : 13/10/2026 à 17:00 CEST
records.application_period: Call opened 16 July 2026 at 09:00 CEST. Step 1 submission and registration closes 13 October 2026 at 17:00 Paris time. Step 1 results are notified mid-February 2027; step 2 runs from end February 2027 (template and IRIS opening) with submission closing end March 2027; selected projects are announced July 2027.
records.description: The AAPG is the ANR's main competitive call and it funds project-based research in every scientific field, including recruitment of doctoral students (contrats doctoraux) and young researchers on successful projects. It runs through five funding instruments: JCJC (young researcher), PRME (single-team project), PRC (collaborative project), PRCE (socio-economic partnership project) and PRCI (bilateral international collaboration project). This is a research-team funding instrument, not an individual scholarship: a doctoral contract is only available to a student recruited onto a project that has been selected for funding.
records.best_fit: Principal investigators and research teams based in a French institution who can submit a project through the IRIS portal by the step 1 deadline and who intend to recruit doctoral students as part of the funded project.
records.eligibility_summary: All scientific communities and all public or private actors involved in French research may apply through one of five funding instruments, choosing one of 57 research axes.
eligibility: Open to all scientific communities and to all public or private actors involved in French research
Covers all scientific fields and all disciplines, including fundamental, exploratory and finalised research

Structured into 57 research axes, each corresponding to a scientific evaluation committee (CES) of the same name: 38 axes within 7 disciplinary domains and 19 axes on cross-cutting trans- or interdisciplinary issues
Coordinators choose the funding instrument (JCJC, PRME, PRC, PRCE, PRCI) when submitting or registering the project; this choice cannot be changed during the selection process
For the PRCE instrument in step 1, no scientific document is required: only the online project characterisation form and the CVs of coordinators and partner scientific leads must be completed

For PRCI collaborations, only the PRCI annexes confirm whether the collaboration is open and under which submission modality; mandatory step 1 registration applies in ANR Lead Agency and non-Lead Agency modalities
coverage: Project-based research funding awarded through the JCJC, PRME, PRC, PRCE and PRCI instruments, which can include recruitment of doctoral contracts
benefits: Additional funding opportunities exist for JCJC and PRCI projects selected in previous editions (Percée JCJC and Jeton MRSEI respectively) to help teams move towards European funding
Projects on the AAPG 2026 complementary list that are resubmitted in AAPG 2027 step 1 are automatically invited to step 2 without scientific committee assessment, subject to eligibility
requirements: Step 1 submission and registration must be completed on the IRIS portal before 13 October 2026 at 17:00 CEST
The research axis, and therefore the scientific evaluation committee, must be chosen at submission and cannot be modified during the selection process
For step 2 invitations, the project must be complete on the submission site by the step 1 closing date and time
For automatic step 2 reinvitation of AAPG 2026 complementary-list projects: same coordinator, same funding instrument, same title and a comparable consortium
The ANR-NSF PRCI collaboration may not be confirmed before the end of step 1 submission and registration; applicants must factor this into their submission strategy
The ANR-FRQ (Franco-Quebec) PRCI collaboration is suspended for the 2027 edition
application_method: Choose the funding instrument and the research axis (and therefore the CES) that matches the project objectives
For PRCE in step 1, complete only the online project characterisation form and the CVs online
For PRCI, consult the dedicated bilateral collaboration annex to confirm the collaboration is open, its modality and its themes
For JCJC, PRME, PRC (and PRCE from step 2), submit the pre-proposal using the published template on the IRIS portal (https://iris.anr.fr/fr/login)
For PRCI submissions where a partner agency is Lead Agency, submit a copy of the project to that foreign agency within the timetable set in the dedicated annex
Complete submission and registration before 13 October 2026 at 17:00 CEST
records.selection_notes: Coordinators choose the research axis and thus the scientific evaluation committee at submission; the choice cannot be changed during the selection process. PRCE step 1 registrations that meet the step 1 eligibility criteria receive an automatic invitation to step 2 without assessment of the scientific value of the registration by the scientific evaluation committees. Step 1 results are notified to coordinators mid-February 2027; a right of reply to reviews opens on IRIS in week 20 of May 2027; the list of projects selected for funding is published in July 2027. PRCI selection requires joint agreement of both funding agencies, each of which ultimately funds the teams of its own country.
records.notes: This is a research-project funding call, not an individual scholarship: there is no personal application route and no scholarship awarded directly to a student. A doctoral contract arises only when a selected project recruits a doctoral student. Funding amounts per instrument are not stated on the call page and must be read in the AAPG 2027 call text (anr-aapg-2027.pdf) and the ANR financial regulations; they are deliberately left unstated here. Projects ranked on the AAPG 2026 complementary list may have to change their partnership to meet the new PRC criteria for the 2027 edition. Applicants selected for funding at the 2026 edition must cancel their AAPG 2027 PRCI registration or JCJC/PRME/PRC submission or PRCE registration by email to aapg.science@anr.fr.

official_details.citizenship_residency: All scientific communities and public or private actors involved in French research; international participation only through the PRCI bilateral collaboration instrument with a partner funding agency.
purpose: Principal call of the Agence nationale de la recherche (ANR): support research on projects in all scientific domains and all disciplines, giving full place to fundamental, exploratory and finalised research, in an approach guided by the curiosity of researchers

As part of reinforcing its action on European issues, accompany researchers in evolving their research strategy from a national dynamic to a European research dynamic, by articulating the expectations of the AAPG instruments with those of Horizon Europe calls
Support research teams moving towards European funding through the complementary Percée JCJC and Jeton MRSEI opportunities for JCJC and PRCI projects selected in previous editions

sdg_requirement_details: The call page states no Sustainable Development Goal requirement. study_type: Project-based research (recherche sur projets) across all scientific domains and disciplines

official_details.degree_award: No degree is awarded by this call. It funds research projects. A doctoral contract (contrat doctoral) arises only where a project selected for funding recruits a doctoral student, and that contract is an employment contract with the recruiting institution, not an award from this record.

covered_expenses: Funding envelopes are awarded per instrument (JCJC, PRME, PRC, PRCE, PRCI) and follow the ANR financial regulations; the ANR also publishes a specific budget annex for French partners that is mandatory for collaborations under a foreign lead agency
not_covered_or_excluded: The call funds projects, not individuals: there is no personal application route and no scholarship or grant awarded directly to a student

Funding amounts per instrument, eligible expenditure rules and any co-funding requirements are not published on the call page; they are set in the call text (anr-aapg-2027.pdf) and in the ANR financial regulations (/fr/rf/), so no figure is asserted here

official_details.international_eligibility: All scientific communities and public or private actors involved in French research may apply. International participation is only possible through the PRCI bilateral collaboration instrument with a partner funding agency, and each agency funds in fine the teams of its own country. A PRCI project may be submitted under one of three modalities: 'ANR Lead Agency' (mandatory ANR step 1 registration, then an ANR step 2 detailed proposal), 'Agence Etr Lead Agency' (no ANR step 1 registration, but a copy of the project as filed with the foreign agency is required within the timetable set in the dedicated annex), or 'Hors modalite Lead Agency' (filed with both agencies on each agency's own calendar, with mandatory ANR step 1 registration).

phd: A doctoral contract (contrat doctoral) can be recruited on a project funded through AAPG 2027, but only by the institution hosting the selected project
The JCJC instrument is aimed at a coordinator who is a young researcher or young researcher-associate (jeune chercheur / jeune chercheuse)
No eligibility rule attaches to individual students: eligibility attaches to the project coordinator and the consortium, so a student cannot apply in their own name

host_requirements: The coordinator must be able to receive and administer the grant through a French research institution, since the call is addressed to actors involved in French research
For PRCI, mandatory step 1 registration with the ANR applies in the 'ANR Lead Agency' and 'Hors modalite Lead Agency' modalities, but not in the 'Agence Etr Lead Agency' modality
In the 'ANR Lead Agency' modality the foreign partner may have to file a copy of the project with its own agency, and the ANR says this must be confirmed with the foreign agency concerned
In the 'Hors modalite Lead Agency' modality the project is filed with both agencies, and each agency assesses it under its own process and calendar
The description of each funding instrument in the call text governs its own submission, eligibility and evaluation modalities
document_format_rules: Pre-proposals must use the official template 'Trame de la pre-proposition' (anr-aapg-2027-Trame-pre-proposition-V1.0.docx); an English pre-proposal form is published as a separate document

For PRCE in step 1, no scientific document is required: only the online completion of the project characterisation form and of the CVs of the coordinators and of the scientific leads of the partners entered online
The 'Annexe budgetaire specifique aux partenaires francais' is mandatory for collaborations under a foreign lead agency
The proposal must be complete on the submission site at the step 1 closing date and time (13 October 2026, 17:00 Paris time) to qualify for a step 2 invitation
Right of reply to reviews is exercised on IRIS, in May 2027 in week 20, by the coordinators of eligible detailed proposals
No file size limit or accepted file type is published on the call page
selection_notes: Projects are assessed by the scientific evaluation committee (CES) that corresponds to the scientific axis chosen at submission

The boundaries of the scientific axes can change between editions of the call, so the ANR invites coordinators to read the axis descriptions carefully in the AAPG 2027 text, including when resubmitting between editions
Each funding instrument has its own submission, eligibility and evaluation specificities, which the ANR says must be read carefully in the AAPG 2027 text

The list of projects selected for funding (JCJC, PRME, PRC and PRCE) is published in July 2027, with notification to coordinators; PRCI results are published from September to December 2027 according to the calendar agreed with the foreign agencies

APG 2026 results for PRCI projects are known from September to December 2026; pending PRCI candidates are invited either to register their project for the 2027 edition (ANR lead agency or hors modalite lead agency modality) or to start a new PRC, PRME, JCJC submission or PRCE registration

common_rejection_risks: Missing the 13 October 2026 17:00 CEST step 1 deadline
Incomplete submission on IRIS at the closing date and time
Changing the research axis or funding instrument during the process
Targeting a PRCI collaboration that is not open, or is suspended (ANR-FRQ), or not yet confirmed (ANR-NSF)
Submitting only on the Campus France-style single portal when a co-deposit with the partner country's institution is required
Failing the new PRC eligibility criteria on international laboratory visibility, involvement of young researchers, and links with socio-economic partners
Choosing a research axis that does not match the project's scientific objectives, which fixes the evaluating committee for the whole process
Attempting to change the funding instrument or the research axis after submission
Registering a PRCI collaboration that is not open for 2027, or that is suspended, or that is not yet confirmed
Failing the new 2027 PRC eligibility criteria on international laboratory visibility, young researcher involvement and socio-economic partnerships
An incomplete submission at 13 October 2026 17:00 Paris time, which also disqualifies a complementary-list project from automatic step 2 invitation
Submitting a PRCE scientific document at step 1 instead of only the online form and CVs

important_advice_for_students: If you are a student, you cannot apply to this call yourself. Apply to a doctoral contract advertised by an institution, and the opportunity appears only once that institution's project has been selected for AAPG funding
If you are a coordinator, lock your research axis and your funding instrument at submission. The ANR states both choices cannot be modified during the selection process

For PRC in the 2027 edition, check the three new eligibility criteria before you submit: international visibility of the laboratories, involvement of young researchers, and links with one or more socio-economic partners
For PRCI, read the dedicated bilateral annex before registering. ANR-FRQ is suspended for 2027 and ANR-NSF may not be confirmed before step 1 closes

If your project was on the AAPG 2026 complementary list, resubmit in step 1 with the same coordinator, instrument and title and a comparable consortium to be invited automatically to step 2, but be ready to change your partnership to meet the new PRC criteria
If you were selected for funding in the 2026 edition, cancel your 2027 registration or submission by e-mail; the ANR states this is obligatory

questions_to_ask_host: Does my host institution's financial service confirm that the budget annex I am submitting matches what IRIS and the financial regulations require for my instrument?

For a PRC project, how do we evidence international laboratory visibility and links with socio-economic partners in a way the CES will accept?
For PRCI, does my foreign partner agency require a parallel filing, and on what calendar, as stated in the dedicated annex?
If my project is selected, how and when does my institution open a doctoral contract recruitment, and what are the salary rules it applies?
What institutional co-funding does my laboratory have to bring, given that the call page publishes no grant amount?

records.description: Inria, the French national institute for research in digital science and technology, recruits PhD students as fixed-term salaried employment contracts rather than as scholarship holders. This post is a 3-year doctoral contract at the Centre Inria d'Universite Cote d'Azur (team TITANE, Sophia Antipolis) with a published gross monthly salary of EUR 2,300, starting 1 December 2026. The work sits inside the JUNN Digital Twin of France and its Territories project, on detecting and analysing 3D change from airborne LidarHD and satellite Digital Surface Model data at national scale.

official_details.citizenship_residency: Not restricted by nationality on the posting; the position is based at the Centre Inria d'Universite Cote d'Azur in Sophia Antipolis, France.
purpose: The goal of this PhD is (i) to develop efficient methods for detecting 3D changes and expressing them with simple geometric shapes, and (ii) to analyze the spatio-temporal distribution of these geometric changes at large scales, from city districts to the entire country

Contribute to the JUNN Digital Twin of France and its Territories project, which uses unprecedented remote sensing data on the whole French territory, including airborne LidarHD campaigns and satellite Digital Surface Models, to update 3D city models over time and to understand the long-term evolution of urban landscapes
Address a key scientific challenge: designing methods for efficiently analysing geometric changes and understanding the evolution of urban attributes such as urban growth and architectural variations

Investigate change detection methods that operate directly on concise geometric primitives such as planes and 3D polygons rather than on 3D point clouds, motivated by efficiency and interoperability, since such primitives feed the building reconstruction methods of the JUNN project for efficient 3D model updates

Develop models for analysing the spatio-temporal distribution of planar shapes at large scales and seek correlations on attributes characterising city evolution in terms of shape, physics or functionality

records.description: Institut Pascal is a Université Paris-Saclay institute that runs thematic scientific programmes lasting typically 2-3 weeks and up to 6 weeks, hosting up to 60 international and national visitors. Selected programmes receive funding for accommodation, on-site catering and part of travel costs for the visiting scientists and students, plus meeting rooms and 26 offices in the Orsay facility. Applications are made by programme organisers as a single PDF, not by individual students.
records.best_fit: Researchers leading a thematic scientific programme (typically from a Paris-Saclay field, from mathematics to life sciences) who can convene international collaborators and students for a multi-week programme and submit a single-PDF proposal by 20 November 2026.
records.eligibility_summary: The call targets thematic scientific programmes, mainly in fields covered by Université Paris-Saclay from mathematics to life sciences, whether theoretical or experimental, that bring scientific communities together to establish new collaborations.

records.name: JSPS Postdoctoral Fellowship for Research in Japan (Standard Program)
records.official_source: Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (JSPS), Overseas Fellowship Division, International Program Department
records.region: Japan (applicants: citizens of any country that has diplomatic relations with Japan, plus Taiwan and Palestine)
records.duration: 12 to 24 months
records.deadline: FY2027 2nd recruitment: April 23, 2027, 5 p.m. JST, submission from the Japanese host institution to JSPS. FY2027 1st recruitment closed on August 28, 2026.
records.application_period: Two open calls per year. FY2027 1st: application deadline August 28, 2026 (5 p.m. JST), results late December 2026, arrival windows April 1 - September 30, 2027, 120 fellowships. FY2027 2nd: application deadline April 23, 2027 (5 p.m. JST), results early August 2027, arrival windows September 1 - November 30, 2027, 120 fellowships.
records.description: JSPS funds postdoctoral researchers from overseas to conduct collaborative research in Japan under the guidance of a Japanese host researcher at a university or other eligible research institution. Financial support is a maintenance allowance of JPY362,000 per month, a round-trip air ticket, a settling-in allowance of JPY200,000, and overseas travel insurance. A Grant-in-Aid for Scientific Research for JSPS Research Fellows can also be applied for through the host institution to cover cooperative research-related expenses. Because this is a research appointment rather than a degree programme, there is no tuition to pay and the award is not presented as tuition funding.
records.best_fit: Researchers who received a PhD within the past six years (maternity and parental leave time is subtracted) and who can secure a host researcher and host institution in Japan before applying.
records.eligibility_summary: Citizens of a country with diplomatic relations with Japan who obtained a doctoral degree on or after April 2 of the year six years before the fiscal year, or who are expected to hold a PhD by the fellowship start date.
eligibility: Be a citizen of a country that has diplomatic relations with Japan (JSPS treats Taiwanese and Palestinian researchers in this manner)

As of April 1 of the fiscal year, have obtained a doctoral degree within six years of the date the fellowship goes into effect (on or after April 2, six years prior to the fiscal year), or who are expected to receive a Ph.D. by the start date of the fellowship period
Whether or not the candidate is employed in a full-time position is not considered
Researchers who obtained their PhD within six years minus time taken for maternity and/or parental leave (every four weeks of leave counted as one month)

Those who have previously been awarded and started a fellowship under the JSPS Postdoctoral Fellowship Program for Research in Japan (Standard, and Pathway to University positions in Japan) are not eligible
Japanese citizens and foreigners with permanent residence status in Japan are not eligible
A selected fellow must submit an original copy of the doctoral degree certificate or diploma before the fellowship starting date
Host researcher must be a full-time researcher at a KAKENHI-eligible institution, eligible to apply for a KAKENHI grant, and each host researcher can submit up to three applications
coverage: Maintenance allowance of JPY362,000 per month
Round-trip air ticket (based on JSPS regulations)
Settling-in allowance of JPY200,000
Overseas travel insurance
Grant-in-Aid for Scientific Research (Grant-in-Aid for JSPS Research Fellow) for cooperative research-related expenses, applied for by the host researcher through their institution
benefits: Settling-in allowance and outbound airfare are not paid to a candidate who has been living in Japan with a mailing address before the fellowship start date
Fellows may spend part of the tenure at another research institution, including one located overseas, when recognised as necessary to advance their research
requirements: Applications must be submitted to JSPS by a host researcher in Japan via the head of their university or institution
Submit the application form using the JSPS Electronic Application System by the deadline designated by the host institution
The JSPS Electronic Application System becomes available approximately two months before the JSPS application period
The host institution must verify that the application is approved by the head of the institution and that the stated requirements will be carried out if approved
application_method: Secure an eligible host researcher and host institution in Japan (JSPS does not introduce host institutions to applicants)

official_details.description: JSPS funds postdoctoral researchers from overseas to conduct collaborative research in Japan under the guidance of their hosts in universities and other research institutions in Japan. Financial support is a maintenance allowance of JPY362,000 per month, a round-trip air ticket, a settling-in allowance of JPY200,000, and overseas travel insurance. A Grant-in-Aid for Scientific Research for JSPS Research Fellows is available for cooperative research-related expenses.
purpose: Enable overseas postdoctoral researchers to conduct collaborative research in Japan under the guidance of a Japanese host researcher, thereby advancing science in Japan and in other countries
Advance the subject research through the host-candidate collaboration, on the published selection policy

Contribute to the training of young researchers and to the formation of new international research networks, as reflected in the published document-review criteria (establishment of new research networks)
Host applicants must have established contact with the candidate in advance and created a concrete research plan, so the fellowship funds an existing collaboration rather than starting one
study_type: Postdoctoral research fellowship

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you obtained your PhD on or after April 2 of the year six years before the fiscal year, adjusting for maternity or parental leave

important_advice_for_students: Do not try to apply on your own. There is no candidate-facing portal: the host researcher enters the application and the head of the host institution transmits it to JSPS. Begin the host relationship first.

Treat the host institution's internal deadline as the real deadline. JSPS itself warns that an institution may set its own deadline more than one month before the JSPS deadline, so waiting for the published April or August date can already be too late.
Ask the host researcher how many applications they still have available, because each host researcher may submit only three applications per recruitment.
Do not budget on the Grant-in-Aid for Scientific Research. It is applied for by the host researcher through the institution and is not a personal entitlement, so it should be treated as contingent.
If you already live in Japan with a mailing address, do not plan on the airfare or the JPY200,000 settling-in allowance; neither is paid in that case.
Check the six-year PhD window yourself before approaching hosts, and remember that every four weeks of maternity or parental leave counts as one month of relief.
Prepare your referee early: the letter must fit on one page and be in English or Japanese, and it travels through the host rather than directly to JSPS.
There is no English test score requirement published for this programme, so do not spend money on one for the application, but expect to work in a Japanese research environment after arrival.
