records.description: This programme brings PhD students and PhD researchers from North America and Europe to Japan to conduct collaborative research under the guidance of a Japanese host for between one and twelve months. Financial support is a maintenance allowance of JPY362,000 per month for PhD holders or JPY200,000 per month for non-PhD holders at the start of the research in Japan, a round-trip air ticket, a settling-in allowance of JPY200,000 for fellows with three or more months of tenure, and overseas travel insurance. A research support allowance for cooperative research-related expenses is applied for by the host researcher. The award is a research fellowship, not a degree scholarship, so no tuition is funded.
records.best_fit: PhD candidates and PhD researchers based in the US, Canada, EU countries, the UK, Switzerland, Norway or Russia who have not previously done research at a Japanese university and can arrange a Japanese host.
records.eligibility_summary: Candidates resident in an eligible North American or European country who obtained a doctoral degree within the past six years as of April 1 of the fiscal year, or who are enrolled in a doctoral course and expect a PhD within two years of the fellowship start date.
eligibility: Be a citizen or permanent resident of an eligible country, or have been engaged in research continuously for at least three years at a university or research institution in an eligible country (eligible countries: US, Canada, EU countries, UK, Switzerland, Norway and Russia); Taiwan and Palestine are also treated as eligible

Have obtained a doctoral degree from a foreign graduate school and, as of April 1 of the fiscal year, be within six years of having obtained that degree, or be currently enrolled in a doctoral course at a foreign graduate school and expect to receive a Ph.D. within two years from the start date of the fellowship period
Whether or not the candidate is employed in a full-time position is not considered

Researchers who have continuously carried out research for three or more years, or obtained their PhD within six years, minus time taken for maternity and/or parental leave (every four weeks counted as one month)
A person who has never engaged in research at universities etc. in Japan would be most preferable

Those who have previously been awarded and started a fellowship under the JSPS Postdoctoral Fellowship for Research in Japan (Standard (P), Short-term (PE), Short-term (PA), or Pathway to University positions in Japan (PU)) are not eligible
Those who have resident cards with mailing addresses in Japan at the application deadline set by JSPS are not eligible
A Japanese citizen who is also a permanent resident of an eligible country is not eligible
A selected fellow needs to submit an original copy of the doctoral degree certificate or diploma, or the prospect certificate if the degree is not yet obtained, before the fellowship starting date
The host researcher must be a full-time researcher at a KAKENHI-eligible institution and may submit up to three applications

The published page does not state any language test score requirement, so treat English proficiency as an inferred practical need rather than a published criterion. official_details.description: This programme provides PhD students or PhD researchers in Europe and North America with opportunities to conduct collaborative research under the guidance of their hosts in universities and other Japanese institutions for a relatively short period of time. Financial support is a maintenance allowance, a round-trip air ticket, a settling-in allowance for tenures of three or more months, overseas travel insurance, and a research support allowance applied for by the host researcher.
purpose: Promote exchange between Japan and the countries of North America and Europe, which is the first stated aim of the published selection policy for this programme
Help advance both the candidate's and the host's research work, as stated in the published selection policy
Require the host and candidate to have established close communication and devised a concrete research plan before the application
Hone the research skills of pre-doctoral candidates, which the published selection policy requires to be addressed in the research plan
Require the host institution to have adequately prepared a system for receiving the candidate
study_type: Short-term research fellowship
Collaborative research under a Japanese host researcher
Open-call recruitment administered by the host institution in Japan
Research appointment, not a taught degree programme
official_details.degree_award: Not a degree programme. This is a research appointment as a JSPS Postdoctoral Fellow, awarded for one to twelve months, and it awards no academic degree. A candidate who has not yet obtained the PhD may be selected on the basis of a prospect certificate. JSPS normally does not issue documents certifying fellowship status; a Fellow needing one, for example for a job application after the fellowship, may request the Application for the Issuance of Certificate (Form 17) at least two weeks before it is needed.

selection_criteria: Selection of applicants (host researcher) and candidates (invited overseas researchers) is done by the JSPS International Program Committee, made up of Japan's frontline researchers
Two-stage selection: a document review in the first stage and a panel review in the second
Document review is conducted by three examiners per application, with experts in the document review section assigned according to the contents of the application
Graduated scoring system on a scale of 1 to 5: 5 superlative, 4 excellent, 3 good, 2 fair, 1 poor
Marks are made on a comprehensive basis, taking into account research achievements, the research plan, estimated research capacity, and future potential of the research
The averaged score in the document review is used as the primary screening criterion in the panel review
Panel review selects a specified number of applicants in each panel review section

The host researcher selects the screening category from the Review Section Table; Review Section Sets pair each review section with the reviewers who screen it, and reviewers are selected in a balanced manner for a diverse range of perspectives
Published selection policy: the implementation of the fellowship contributes to promoting exchange between Japan and countries of North America and Europe
Published selection policy: the fellowship helps to advance both the candidate's and the host's research work
Published selection policy: the host and candidate have established close communication and devised a concrete research plan
Published selection policy: the host institution has adequately prepared a system for receiving the candidate
Published selection policy: in the research plan, consideration is given to honing the research skills of pre-doctoral candidates
Published selection policy: as much as possible, preference is not given to host institution or field of specialization in making selections
Published selection policy: not only the score of the document review but also the examiners' reasons and comments are to be given adequate consideration
Published selection policy: two selection judgements are made, Selected and Not-selected

Integrity rules: any reviewer with a potential conflict of interest is removed from the Review Committee for the relevant review, and all Review Committee members are obliged to comply with a confidentiality and non-disclosure agreement

important_advice_for_students: Do not try to apply on your own. There is no candidate-facing portal: the host researcher enters the application and the head of the host institution transmits it to JSPS. Start the host relationship first, and note that this programme publishes three rounds a year, so a missed host deadline only costs you one round, not a whole year.

Check the country rule carefully before anything else. Citizenship alone is not the only route: three or more continuous years of research at an institution in an eligible country also qualifies, but Japanese resident-card holders with a Japanese mailing address at the JSPS deadline are excluded outright.
Plan the length of your stay deliberately. A tenure under three months forfeits the settling-in allowance, and a pre-doctoral candidate is paid JPY200,000 per month rather than JPY362,000.

The published selection policy says preference is not given to host institution or field of specialization, and it requires the research plan to show how a pre-doctoral candidate's research skills will be honed. Write the plan accordingly rather than assuming prestige of the host carries weight.
The published selection policy states that a person who has never done research at a Japanese university would be most preferable. If you have, do not hide it, but do not lead with it either.
The Research Support Allowance is applied for by the host researcher, not by you. Ask the host whether they intend to apply, since it is contingent and affects what research budget you can plan.
No English test score is published for this programme, so do not spend money on one for the application.

important_advice_for_students: Do not treat February to March as your real deadline. On the Embassy Track the embassy sets an earlier local deadline and runs its own screening before NIIED ever sees your file, so you are managing two deadlines, not one.

If you want to avoid the embassy's screening and deadline entirely, the University Track is a direct application to a designated university. The trade-off is that university Track options are narrower for some categories: R-GKS is Type B only, and R&D and Global Network are limited to their own named institution lists.

Watch the GKS notices board rather than waiting for NIIED to email you. For the 2026 cycle the board carried dated result notices in May, June and July, a separate Embassy Track final choice of university notice, and a notice revising the schedule for issuance of invitation letters. Those notices, not the overview page, are where the binding dates live.

Do not budget from this overview page. It names four benefits (airfare, Korean language training fees, tuition, monthly allowances) but publishes no allowance figure and does not say whether medical insurance, a settlement allowance or a thesis allowance is included. The annual guideline is the only place to settle that.

If you are an engineering or science applicant, the R&D specialisation is the industrial-field route and is available only at Master's and doctoral level. If you are a humanities or social science applicant looking for English delivery, Global Network is the only route, and it is Master's degree only with no Korean language training.
Global Network is described as mainly inviting experts and key figures with lectures mainly in English. Read the annual guideline before assuming an ordinary admissions route into it.
The 80% GPA rule is stated as an average from your most recent academic programme. Check how that maps to your own grading scale before assuming you qualify.

purpose: An inbound scholarship supporting global talents to complete Master's and doctoral programs in Korea, published as 'For Next Generation Global Leaders'
The programme empowers promising global leaders by offering full tuition and living expenses as they pursue Master's or doctoral degrees at top Korean universities

Unlike traditional Korean scholarships aimed at supporting domestic students abroad, the programme uniquely welcomes outstanding individuals from around the world to study in Korea and build meaningful connections with Korean society
Through academic coursework and immersive experiences including industry visits and cultural programs, awardees gain in-depth knowledge of Korea's economy, society and values
As they complete their degrees, awardees are equipped to become globally-minded leaders who bridge their home countries with Korea and contribute to a more interconnected world

Umbrella rationale published by the Foundation: POSCO Global Scholarship is founded on the belief that deeper mutual understanding among individuals leads to stronger global connections, ultimately contributing to peace and shared prosperity around the world
The Foundation operates the programme to promote mutual understanding through global talent exchange and collaboration, and to help build a global network of next-generation leaders

important_advice_for_students: Start with university admission, not with the scholarship. Admission to a designated graduate school is stage 01 of the Foundation's own five-stage procedure, so an application strategy that starts with the Foundation cannot work.

The single most common failure point is forgetting the recommendation. The applicant cannot submit it; the graduate school does. Ask the department, in writing, when it will send the recommendation to the Foundation, and check back in November rather than assuming.

Treat the eligible-country and eligible-university lists as provisional. The Foundation marks both as tentative and separately marks the 20-student quota as subject to change, so confirm the current year's lists with asiafellowship@postf.org before you commit to a university.

Do not plan to arrive in January. Every Foundation stage date is published with a tilde, from around November to around February, and the only fixed date in the cycle is the March certificate award ceremony.

Budget from the caps, not the headline. Tuition is full only for 4 semesters (Master's) or 6 semesters (doctoral or integrated), and living expenses only for 22 or 36 months. If your programme runs longer, the extra time is your own cost.
Insurance is handled: the National Health Insurance premium is a published benefit. Airfare is not on the published benefit list, so fund your own travel.
Both eligible-country and eligible-university lists are published as tentative on the official site, so do not rely on a list you read from a secondary source.

records.description: A complementary support awarded jointly by the OAS and Mexico's Secihti to students who already hold a Secihti National Scholarship for a full-time postgraduate programme in Mexico. The OAS contribution is a single payment of USD 1,200 for settling-in expenses in Mexico, paid in Mexican pesos at the official exchange rate on the day OAS deposits it, and the number of supports depends on OAS funds. Secihti adds its monthly support under the Secihti 2026 National Scholarship Scale plus ISSSTE medical service. The call does not establish tuition, travel or full living-cost coverage, so this is not full funding.
records.best_fit: Non-Mexican nationals of OAS Member States who are already current holders of a Secihti National Scholarship for a full-time postgraduate programme in one of the listed STEM, health, biotechnology or agricultural sciences areas in Mexico.
records.eligibility_summary: Applicants must already be current Secihti National Scholarship holders admitted and enrolled in a full-time postgraduate programme in a listed subject area, and be nationals of an OAS Member State other than Mexico.
eligibility: Declarar en su perfil único tener la nacionalidad de alguno de los Estados Miembros de la OEA, con excepción de México.

Haber obtenido una Beca Secihti Nacional in one of the six named calls: Becas Nacionales para Estudios de Posgrado programas elegibles 2025 segundo periodo; Becas Nacionales para Estudios de Posgrado en Humanidades y Ciencias de la Conducta 2025 segundo periodo; Becas Nacionales para Estudios de Posgrado en Entidades Federativas con Mayor Rezago Social 2025 segundo periodo; Becas Nacionales para Estudios de Posgrado para Especialidades en Áreas de la Salud 2025 segundo periodo; Becas Nacionales para Estudios de Posgrado en programas que pertenezcan a las áreas de Físico-Matemáticas y Ciencias de la Tierra, Biología y Química, Ingenierías y Desarrollo Tecnológico 2025 segundo periodo; or Becas Nacionales para Estudios de Posgrado 2026, término de referencia A, programas elegibles escolarizados, primer periodo.
Ser persona becaria nacional vigente en un programa de posgrado escolarizado.

Estar admitido e inscrito en las áreas de Física, Matemáticas y Ciencias de la Tierra, Biología y Química, Ingenierías, Medicina y Ciencias de la Salud (a excepción de la formación de especialidades y subespecialidades médicas), Biotecnología y Ciencias Agropecuarias.
coverage: OAS: single contribution of USD 1,200 for gastos de instalación (settling-in expenses) in Mexico, paid in Mexican pesos at the official exchange rate of the day OAS deposits to the beneficiary's bank account.
Secihti: monthly economic support according to the 'Tabulador de Becas Nacionales 2026'.
Secihti: medical service provided by ISSSTE, on registering as a beneficiary under ISSSTE rules.
benefits: The OAS portion is explicitly stated to be independent from the scholarship granted by Secihti.
requirements: The beneficiary must send the information and documentation that the OAS requests for formalisation and disbursement, on time and in full.

Under article 17-A of the Ley Federal de Procedimiento Administrativo, a failure to send that information triggers a single emailed prevención with a term of no fewer than five business days; if it is not corrected, the support may be cancelled and reassigned.
application_method: There is no public application form for new applicants: participation requires already being a current national scholarship holder selected under one of the calls listed in the eligibility section.
Secihti validates the applications of persons who were beneficiaries under the listed calls and sends the compliant list to the OAS on 28 August 2026.
The OAS Award Committee deliberates on 3 September 2026 and Secihti and the OAS notify selected students directly between 4 and 10 September 2026.
Results of the assigned applications are published on the OAS website and notified by email from both Secihti and the OAS.
Formalisation is carried out by signing the corresponding instrument between the OAS and the selected beneficiary.
Disbursement is made once the support has been formalised, following the timetable and procedure the OAS communicates by email.
records.selection_notes: The OAS selects among the Secihti national scholarship holders using ten published criteria: being admitted and enrolled in a listed subject area; being a current national scholarship holder in a full-time postgraduate programme selected by Secihti; geographic balance by country of origin; the applicant's country Human Development Index; gender; area of study; geographic distribution of the host institution in Mexico; level of study (doctorate over master's); dual nationality and residence in Mexico; and proportion of candidates per country. The number of supports depends on the availability of OAS funds.
records.notes: This is NOT an award first-time applicants can enter into. The only published entry route is already holding a current Secihti National Scholarship, and the applicant's name must have been on the list Secihti sent to the OAS on 28 August 2026. As of the 2026-10-01 verification date the selection, notification and formalisation steps in the published calendar had already run (3-18 September 2026); the published process close date is 30 November 2026, so what remains open is the finalisation of the process and the documentation/disbursement steps, not fresh selection. Applicants who are not existing Secihti national scholarship holders should treat this record as not applicable to them. Tuition is not covered by anything published here, Secihti does not handle immigration procedures for the beneficiary or their economic dependents, support can be cancelled if a restriction or incompatibility is found, names of beneficiaries are published in the Secihti register, and the award can be audited during the award and for 5 years after it ends.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you are already a current Secihti National Scholarship holder under one of the six named calls; if not, this programme is not open to you.
Confirm your programme is a full-time (escolarizado) postgraduate programme in one of the listed subject areas.
Confirm that medical specialties and subspecialties are not your programme type, as they are excluded.
Check whether you have previously received an OAS complementary support, which is disqualifying, and whether you have any outstanding obligation or debt under programme S190.
Declare your nationality of an OAS Member State other than Mexico on your single Secihti profile (perfil único), because that is where the call requires nationality to be declared.
Prepare to respond fast to the OAS documentation request once formalisation starts, allowing at least five business days.
Keep your Secihti beneficiary file clean: any compliance-incurrence report or debt under programme S190 is an explicit bar, and the OAS may cancel an award already granted.
important_advice_for_students: Do not spend any time on this 'application'. There is nothing to file. The only route is to be a current Secihti national scholarship holder whose name Secihti put on the list it sent to the OAS on 28 August 2026. If you are not already inside the Secihti system, this programme cannot help you.

Understand what you are actually getting: a one-off USD 1,200 for settling-in expenses in Mexico, paid in pesos at whatever the exchange rate is on the deposit date. It is not a tuition payment and not a living stipend. Budget your programme on the Secihti scholarship itself, not on this top-up.

The published selection and notification stages are already over. The deliberación was 3 September 2026 and direct notification ran 4 to 10 September 2026, both before this record's verification date. The 30 November 2026 date is the close of the process, not a deadline you can still apply against. If you are reading this for the first time, check your email and your Secihti file rather than your calendar.

Treat the emailed prevención as final. Article 17-A gives you exactly one notice, with a correction term the OAS sets and which may not be shorter than five business days. Miss it and the support is cancelled and reassigned to someone who was not favoured for lack of budget.

Your name will be published. Beneficiary names go into the padrón on Secihti's website under the transparency law. If you send anything you consider confidential, you must declare it in writing and say which documents or sections and why; and if you send classifiable information anyway, the consequences are entirely on you.
Know that the audit trail is long: the support can be reviewed or audited during the award and for five years after it ends, without needing your authorisation.

Do not expect the OAS to help with immigration. The call states in terms that Secihti does not intervene in the migratory situation of the national scholarship holder or their economic dependents, so that is entirely yours to arrange.

Two factors are published that people forget: doctoral candidates are ranked above master's candidates, and the geographic distribution of your host institution in Mexico is itself a criterion. If you have any choice of campus, it is not neutral.
common_rejection_risks: Not being a current Secihti national scholarship holder under one of the six listed calls.
Mexican nationality, which is explicitly excluded.
Enrolled in a medical specialty or subspecialty, which is excluded.
Having received an OAS complementary support previously.
Having an outstanding compliance report or debt under programme S190.
Not being admitted and enrolled in one of the listed subject areas.
Being a master's candidate when doctoral candidates are ranked first on the published level-of-study criterion.
Failing to send the documentation requested by the OAS within the emailed prevención window, which can lead to cancellation and reassignment.
estimated_uncovered_costs: All tuition and mandatory fees: nothing published here covers them.
Round-trip airfare and any travel costs.
The balance of monthly living costs above whatever the Secihti monthly scale and the one-time USD 1,200 provide; the monthly figure is not published in this call.
Visa, immigration and relocation costs, which Secihti explicitly does not handle.
Costs for economic dependents.

Bank account details, because the OAS credits the peso equivalent of the USD 1,200 to the beneficiary's bank account at the exchange rate of the deposit date.
The specific document set the OAS requires for formalisation: not enumerated in the call, so it must be requested from scholarships@oas.org before the window opens.
Any material you consider confidential must be marked as such in writing, naming the documents or sections and the reason, because everything else received is public under the transparency laws.

records.description: The GS/OAS and the Universidad del Desarrollo in Chile fund USD 3,400 of the USD 3,800 total course fee for a 4-month online certificate in Global Innovation and Entrepreneurship (dLab Global 2026), focused on SDG 13 climate action. The selected candidate remains responsible for USD 400 of the course fee, plus study materials or equipment, internet access, and any additional fees not included in the offer. Living costs, travel and insurance are not addressed at all in the announcement, so this is not full funding and there is no stipend to live on.
records.best_fit: Young professionals from OAS Member States other than Chile who have a business management background, a strong interest in innovation and entrepreneurship, and can commit about 4.5 hours a week in English to a fully online course.
records.eligibility_summary: Applicants must be citizens or permanent residents of an active OAS Member State other than Chile, be proficient in English, have a strong business management background, and commit to paying the remaining USD 400 course fee.
eligibility: Be a citizen or permanent resident of an OAS member state, except Chile.
Have a strong interest in innovation and entrepreneurship.
Innovative resilience building business concepts closely linked to climate or environmental resilience is especially encouraged, or one that addresses a need in the market.
Can 'think outside the box,' exhibit critical thinking skills, and have a quest for discovery or investigative learning.

Commit to covering the remaining course fee of USD 400 to the UDD.
coverage: USD 3,400 of the total course fee, contributed jointly by the GS/OAS and the University, out of a total cost of USD 3,800.

records.english_requirement: Applicants whose native language is not English must submit an official transcript confirming completion of studies at an English-speaking university or college within the past five years; or TOEFL 570+ (paper), 230+ (computer), or 79+ (internet-based/IBT); or IELTS 6.5 or equivalent.
application_method: Prepare all supporting documents combined into one single PDF file not exceeding 5 MB, in English or with an official English translation.
Complete the OAS online scholarship application, noting that the system permits only one document upload.
Submit the complete application package with all supporting documents via the OAS link no later than 31 January 2027.
If pre-selected, respond to the email contact and take part in an interview with the scholarship selection committee in English, if necessary.
If finally selected, sign the formal OAS acceptance form after being contacted by email with the scholarship offer and acceptance instructions.
records.selection_notes: A specialized OAS and UDD committee selects the recipients. Elements considered in awarding the scholarships are geographic distribution of the candidates, the applicant's profile including education and project outline and recommendation, the applicant's potential impact on completion of the course, and gender distribution. A selection committee pre-selects participants on that profile; pre-selected participants may be interviewed in English. Results are published at www.oas.org/scholarships by February 2027, and unsuccessful applicants are not contacted.
records.notes: This is a fee-reduction award, not a living stipend: the scholarship covers USD 3,400 of a USD 3,800 course fee and the recipient must find USD 400 plus study materials, equipment and internet access themselves. No living cost, travel or health insurance funding is published, so applicants must not budget this as full funding. Not eligible: current OAS scholarship recipients, GS/OAS staff and their immediate family, GS/OAS consultants, and permanent OAS staff and their immediate family. The recipient may decline the scholarship before the program start date without financial penalty, but declining after that date without proof of force majeure may require repayment of all funds awarded. The GS/OAS reserves the right to cancel this scholarship announcement at any time during the process.

official_details.description: The General Secretariat of the Organization of American States and Universidad del Desarrollo in Chile award scholarships to pursue a certificate in Global Innovation and Entrepreneurship through the dLab Global 2026 programme. The total course fee is USD 3,800, of which the GS/OAS and the University contribute USD 3,400 per selected candidate, leaving USD 400 for the selected candidate. The overriding theme is sustainability and climate change, focused on UN SDG 13. Study materials, equipment and internet access are not covered.
purpose: The General Secretariat of the OAS (GS/OAS) and Universidad del Desarrollo decided to support outstanding individuals from the Americas by awarding scholarships to pursue a certificate in Global Innovation and Entrepreneurship

The overriding theme of the course is Sustainability/Climate Change and how innovation can be used to reduce the effects of what is happening, as well as helping to prevent and mitigate this phenomenon

The programme focuses on the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, namely SDG 13, which focuses on taking urgent action to combat climate change and its impacts, and the innovative projects developed centre on this subject

The GS/OAS supports Member States in creating policies and implementing programs that promote the development of human capabilities at all educational levels, strengthening democratic values and security within the framework of regional integration
Participants are connected with the innovation and entrepreneurship ecosystem at UDD and in Chile, with experts in innovation invited to speak about their projects

important_advice_for_students: Get the single-file rule right first. Only one upload is permitted and every required document must be inside one PDF of no more than 5 MB. Splitting files across uploads, or exceeding 5 MB after scanning photos at full resolution, is the most common way to fail here.

Translate everything properly. Every document must be in English or carry an official English translation, and incomplete applications are not accepted at all, so a missing translation is a rejection, not a request for more information.

The English test route is flexible and cheaper than people assume. If you completed studies at an English-speaking university or college within the past five years, an official transcript is accepted instead of a test score, which saves you the exam fee if you qualify.

Budget for the USD 400 yourself and prove it. The scholarship covers USD 3,400 of USD 3,800, and you must additionally fund study materials, equipment and internet access, none of which the award touches.

Read the eligibility criteria as a filter, not a formality. Four of the eleven published conditions are behavioural: 'think outside the box' and critical thinking, a quest for discovery, demonstrable ability to lead and inspire, and 4.5 hours a week for a whole semester. If you cannot commit the time, do not apply.

Expect an interview, and expect it in English. Pre-selected candidates are contacted by email to take part in an interview with the selection committee in English if necessary, so treat English interview fluency as part of the assessment, not just the written evidence.

The course is anchored on UN SDG 13. If you read the announcement and cannot say how your project touches climate change or climate resilience, you are not the profile they are selecting for, and the business concept statement is where that has to come through.
Do not wait for feedback if you are rejected. The announcement states that unsuccessful applicants will not be contacted.

records.description: The SG/OAS awards tuition discounts for online postgraduate study with UNIR (Spain), the Escuela de Posgrado Peruana de NEWMAN (Peru) and UNIR Mexico. Up to 885 places are offered, with a 60% discount on total tuition for official master's programmes and official degrees, and a 50% discount for UNIR Formación Permanente programmes, applicable only to the value of the study programme. Admission fees, translation and notarisation, study materials, titulation and degree-awarding procedures, and any other cost not listed are explicitly excluded, and recipients must personally demonstrate the financial capacity to cover the uncovered programme costs, so this is not full funding.

application_method: Step 1: Follow the admission process for the chosen programme directly with the institution, submitting all documentation the institution requires, and pay the admission fee.

Step 2: Once admitted and in receipt of the institution's application letter (carta de aplicacion), the applicant is automatically considered a candidate for the OAS-UNIR, EP NEWMAN and UNIR Mexico scholarship; there is no separate scholarship application form.
Step 3: UNIR, EP NEWMAN, UNIR Mexico and the OAS form a specialised committee to select the scholarship holders.
Step 4: Await publication of results at www.oea.org/becas, announced from November 2026 for the 2a convocatoria.

Step 5: Only selected candidates are contacted by email by UNIR, EP NEWMAN and UNIR Mexico with the scholarship offer and acceptance instructions; after accepting, the scholarship holder starts the corresponding payment procedures with the chosen institution.
records.selection_notes: A specialised committee of UNIR, EP NEWMAN, UNIR Mexico and the OAS selects the scholarship holders, considering the geographic distribution of candidates according to the needs of Member States as reflected in the UNDP Human Development Index, the academic profile and merit and academic credentials, the applicant's potential impact on completing the programme, and gender distribution.
records.notes: This is a tuition discount only and it does not cover the whole fee, so applicants must not treat it as full funding. The 2a convocatoria deadlines fall between 19 and 30 October 2026, so the UNIR and EP NEWMAN lines close first on 19 October 2026. Excluded from eligibility: SG/OAS officials, persons under contract by results with the SG/OAS, Permanent Mission staff, and relatives of all of the above. Nicaraguan nationals and permanent legal residents are excluded. Applicants cannot study in their own country of origin. The call states programme costs shown in the document are orientative and may be lower in some countries, and it repeatedly warns that neither the OAS nor the institutions take responsibility for recognition, legalisation, homologation or convalidacion of the resulting title in the applicant's country of country of origin. The scholarship is conditional on academic performance, and it applies only to the value of the study programme. The SG/OAS reserves the right to cancel this announcement at any point in the process. The document's benefits section refers to a 'Responsabilidades del Becario' section on page 27, but the official PDF available at this URL contains only 10 pages, so that section could not be read.

records.description: The KAUST Fellowship is awarded automatically to admitted graduate students at King Abdullah University of Science and Technology in Thuwal, Saudi Arabia. The published package covers full tuition and bench fees (stated as worth up to USD $35,000 per year), a monthly stipend (stated as worth USD $20,000 per year for M.S. students and USD $25,000 to $30,000 per year for Ph.D. students depending on qualifications and academic progress), base on-campus accommodation, health insurance for students and eligible dependents living on campus, and relocation support covering visa, relocation and travel costs. KAUST states the total value of the Fellowship at between $70k and $80k per year depending on the student's situation.

records.english_requirement: IELTS 7.0 overall with at least 6.5 in all individual sections (IELTS Online accepted), or TOEFL iBT 5.0 overall with at least 4.5 in all individual sections (KAUST Admissions code 4107; TOEFL Home Edition accepted), or PTE Academic 71 overall with at least 67 in all individual sections, or Cambridge C1 Advanced/C2 Proficiency 185 overall with at least 176 in all individual sections. records.selection_notes: Five-stage process: submission, Admissions team document review, faculty review committee evaluation and ranking against other applicants with shortlisting for interviews, academic interview and/or test, then decision. Admission review is holistic, considering academic achievements and personal qualities such as motivation and potential impact in the scientific community. All admission decisions are final and will not be reconsidered, and KAUST states it cannot provide individual feedback on specific applications.
records.notes: Relocation assistance is only for each student's initial move to KAUST and their return home upon graduation. Some students with external sponsorship or funding may not be eligible for the KAUST Fellowship. Eligible students who request a housing upgrade pay an additional fee. An English proficiency score is not required if the applicant's degree was completed by in-person study at an accredited institution in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, Ireland, Australia or New Zealand, or if the applicant previously completed a degree taken at KAUST's campus in Thuwal; distance learning, satellite campuses, joint programs and branch institutions outside those countries do not qualify for the exemption. Applicants may submit without an English score but must meet the minimum before enrolment. Saudi nationals and PhD students scoring IELTS 6.5 / TOEFL 4.5 / PTE 64 / Cambridge 176 may be admitted on condition of taking the Academic English Language Communication Course in their first year. KAUST does not accept Medium of Instruction certificates, the Duolingo English Test (except for Visiting Student applicants), TOEFL MyBest superscores, or IELTS One Skill Retake results. If accepted, there is a limited time to respond to secure the place or the decision may be withdrawn.

records.description: MBZUAI's graduate funding is not a single named scholarship but a University-and-faculty funding model under which funded M.Sc. and Ph.D. students receive free tuition fees, a monthly stipend, one return airfare each year to their home country, health insurance for the approved funding period, and a University-sponsored UAE residence visa and Emirates ID where eligible. M.Sc. students are fee-paying by default and funding is secured through a faculty advisor-sponsored research or teaching assistantship, or an approved government scholarship for UAE nationals, with merit-based funding considered during the admissions review process. The Master in Applied Artificial Intelligence is a fee-based programme and is not eligible for University or faculty-sponsored funding.

records.name: HBKU Graduate Tuition Waiver and Stipend
records.official_source: Hamad Bin Khalifa University (HBKU), a member of Qatar Foundation for Education, Science, and Community Development
records.region: Qatar (Qatari, resident and international graduate applicants)
records.duration: Stipend duration of 45 months for PhD programmes and 21 months for Master's programmes
records.deadline: Online graduate admission application opens to the public 1 October 2026; admission application deadline for international graduate applicants 1 February 2027; admission application deadline for Qatari and resident applicants who wish to apply for funding 15 March 2027
records.application_period: Online applications open to the public on 1 October 2026 and close on 1 February 2027 for international graduate applicants. Qatari and resident applicants who wish to apply for funding have a later deadline of 15 March 2027. records.description: HBKU graduate scholarships may include a tuition waiver applied to reduce tuition costs and a stipend paid directly to the student, and HBKU states that graduate students receiving a stipend would generally also be provided with a tuition waiver. Tuition waivers are standardised across HBKU and range from 100% for PhD STEM and PhD SHAPE and S.J.D. programmes down to 0% for LL.M. programmes, MS Economics and certificate programmes. Stipends are awarded to selected graduate students, with published monthly and annual rates for Qatari, international and local PhD and Master's students, over durations of 45 months for PhD and 21 months for Master's. Awards depend on the availability of funds, are not guaranteed, and are made on a merit or need basis only.

records.eligibility_summary: Tuition waivers and stipend awards at HBKU depend on the availability of funds, are not guaranteed, and are awarded only on a merit or need basis; stipends are awarded to full-time graduate students serving as research assistants and/or teaching assistants.

records.selection_notes: There is a preliminary application review by the HBKU admissions team for completeness and eligibility, followed by assessment by the relevant college. Scholarships are not awarded automatically to admitted students: HBKU states they are offered based on merit or financial need and available funds, and they are reviewed annually depending on academic progress and available funds.
records.notes: Students are responsible for covering the cost of their housing, whether in Qatar Foundation dormitory facilities or external accommodation; this expense is paid from the monthly stipend or personal funds, and HBKU does not provide direct payment for student housing. Meal plans are not separately included; the stipend is a fixed amount meant to cover general living expenses including meals. Stipend awards do not depend on the student's marital status or the number of family dependents. Stipends for local students are limited. Stipends funded from external sources, including research grants, are excluded from the published rates. Self-sponsored graduate students are only eligible for a discounted tuition rate of 2,000 QAR per credit hour based on financial need, and these scholarship guidelines do not apply to students funded by external sources. Receipt of external funding may affect eligibility. Deferral of admission may affect scholarship eligibility. LL.M. programmes, MS Economics and certificate programmes carry a 0% tuition waiver.

records.description: The UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs runs a scholarship programme for Emirati students to study a Bachelor's degree at one of the world's top universities approved by MOFA, specialising in fields that meet the needs of the UAE diplomatic corps. MOFA states in its FAQ that the programme covers all tuition costs in accordance with the programme's policies, and the applicant must already hold an unconditional direct academic acceptance from an approved university indicating the programme start and end dates and the total cost. The programme is not a general study-abroad scholarship: it carries a service obligation, requiring the holder to join the MOFA diplomatic corps for a period equivalent to the number of academic years covered by the scholarship and to join the Anwar Gargash Diplomatic Academy upon graduation.
records.best_fit: Emirati nationals aged 17 to 21 (up to 22 at the time of application) with a high school diploma meeting the published percentage thresholds, an IELTS Academic score of 6.5 or equivalent, and an unconditional offer from a MOFA-approved university, who are willing to enter the UAE diplomatic corps.

records.notes: This is a service-obligation scholarship, not free money to study anywhere: applicants must agree to join the UAE diplomatic corps at MOFA for a period equivalent to the number of academic years covered by the scholarship, and must agree to join the Anwar Gargash Diplomatic Academy upon graduation. Only UAE nationals may apply, and only MOFA-approved universities are eligible, so an applicant who already has an offer from an unlisted institution cannot use this programme. Male applicants must have completed or been exempt from national service. Applicants who defer or want to change their major or country of study must inform the relevant programme officer at the Ministry and notify the cultural attaché in the country of study. The published page states that MOFA covers all tuition costs but does not publish any statement on living costs, accommodation, airfare or a stipend.

records.name: NL Scholarship (formerly Holland Scholarship)
records.official_source: Study in NL (Nuffic) — financed by the Dutch Ministry of Education, Culture and Science and Dutch higher education institutions
records.region: Netherlands (applicants from outside the European Economic Area)
records.deadline: The application for the academic year 2026-2027 opened on 1 November 2025. Please check the website of the institution you want to apply to for the specific deadline(s).
records.application_period: Annual cycle: applications for an academic year open on 1 November of the preceding calendar year and close on institution-specific dates earlier in the year. The central page published the 2026-2027 opening date of 1 November 2025 and had not yet published a 2027-2028 opening date when checked.
records.description: The NL Scholarship is the Dutch national scholarship programme for bachelor and master students from outside the European Economic Area. It is financed by the Dutch Ministry of Education, Culture and Science together with Dutch research universities and universities of applied sciences. Study in NL states the scholarship amounts to € 5,000 and is paid in the first year of studies, and explicitly notes that it is not a full-tuition scholarship. Institutions set their own application deadlines and their own amount tiers, so the value and the deadline both depend on the institution you apply to.
records.best_fit: Non-EEA nationals applying for a full-time bachelor's or master's programme at one of the listed participating Dutch research universities or universities of applied sciences who can fund the remainder of tuition and living costs themselves.
records.eligibility_summary: Applicants must be of non-EEA nationality, be applying for a full-time bachelor's or master's programme at a participating Dutch institution, meet that institution's own requirements, and not hold a degree from a Dutch education institution.
eligibility: Your nationality is non-EEA.
You are applying for a full-time bachelor's or master's programme at one of the participating Dutch higher education institutions.
You meet the specific requirements of the institution of your choice. You can find these on the website of the institution.
You do not have a degree from an education institution in the Netherlands.
Radboud University: You must not be eligible for the lower EU/EEA tuition fee for other reasons.

Radboud University: You must have (will obtain) a Bachelor's degree achieved outside the Netherlands, have no degrees achieved in the Netherlands and did not receive any previous education in the Netherlands (exchange programmes excluded, provided that they are part of the Bachelor's degree achieved outside the Netherlands).
Radboud University: You must meet the English language proficiency requirement for the Master's programme of your choice.
Radboud University: You must be able to comply with the conditions for obtaining a visa for the Netherlands.
Utrecht University: You must not be eligible for statutory tuition fees.

Utrecht University: You must never have been enrolled at an educational institution in the Netherlands (if you only took part in an exchange programme in the Netherlands, this does not make you ineligible).
coverage: A one-off grant of € 5,000 paid in the first year of studies (Study in NL and Radboud University figures).
Nothing else. Study in NL states it is not a full-tuition scholarship; Radboud University states the costs of living and studying in the Netherlands are not covered.
benefits: At Radboud University the NL Scholarship is always combined with the Radboud Scholarship Programme (RSP): applicants must also apply for the RSP, and can be awarded both or just the RSP, never the NLS alone.
Utrecht University publishes three award tiers rather than one: €5,000, €10,000 and €15,000, all paid in the first year of studies even for a two-year programme.
Nuffic states the programme is made available jointly with 47 Dutch higher education institutions, which will grant scholarships to 2,112 students per academic year.
requirements: Apply for an NL Scholarship-eligible programme at a participating institution and meet that institution's admission and scholarship requirements.
Utrecht University: your application must be submitted before 1 February, 23:59 CET; the application portal closes at that time and selection only starts after the deadline.
Utrecht University: results are aimed to be published by mid-April.

Utrecht University: you must demonstrate you can cover the remaining costs by completing the Statement of Financial Resources, showing a realistic plan covering the full nominal duration of the Master's programme.

Radboud University: your OSIRIS application must be submitted by 31 January 2027, 23:59 CET at the latest, and must be complete by 14 February 2027, 23:59 CET at the latest; incomplete applications will not be considered for scholarship selection.
Radboud University: proof of English proficiency should be handed in before the 14 February 2027 deadline.
Radboud University: the decision is communicated around mid-April 2027 (date subject to change).
Nuffic operates an integrity Code of Conduct; the programme may not be involved in financial misconduct, tax or social security default, money laundering, terrorist financing or related conduct.
application_method: Choose a participating Dutch institution and an NL Scholarship-eligible programme (not every programme participates).
Apply for admission to that programme through the institution's own application system.
Radboud University: indicate during the OSIRIS application procedure for a Master's programme that you wish to apply for an NL Scholarship.

Utrecht University: submit the application for an NL Scholarship-eligible MA programme, log in to your OSIRIS Online Application account, locate 'NL Scholarship' under your dashboard, click 'View/Edit' for the scholarship linked to your chosen programme, open the application form, answer all required questions and submit.
Meet your institution's published deadline and completeness deadline.
Upload all required documents, including the institutional financial-plans form where required.
Await the selection outcome, published by the institution after its deadline.
records.selection_notes: Utrecht University assesses applications on the academic background shown in the master's programme application, the motivation explaining the relevance of the time in the Netherlands and at Utrecht University to future goals, and the quality and feasibility of the financial plan. Radboud University assesses on academic excellence (outstanding study results, relevance of the previous degree to the programme, ranking of the university where previous degrees were obtained) and ambition (quality and relevance of the motivation letter, promise shown by achievements, life experience and extracurricular activities such as internships or volunteering), with each faculty considering its own applicants individually. Admission to the programme and selection for the scholarship are two separate processes.
records.notes: This is not full funding and should never be budgeted as such: Study in NL states it is not a full-tuition scholarship and Radboud University states explicitly that the costs of living and studying in the Netherlands are not covered. At Radboud University the award is limited to one year and can only be received once. The programme was renamed from Holland Scholarship to NL Scholarship in June 2023, so older material under the old name may be out of date. Selection for the scholarship is separate from admission to the programme — an admission offer does not imply a scholarship. Utrecht University requires applicants to prove they can cover the full remaining cost of the programme.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your nationality is non-EEA and that you are not eligible for the lower EU/EEA or statutory tuition fee.
Confirm you hold no degree from a Dutch education institution and have never been enrolled at one outside an exchange programme.
Pick a participating institution from the Study in NL list for the relevant academic year, then confirm that the specific programme you want actually participates â€” not every programme does.
Go to that institution's own scholarship page immediately, because it holds the only real deadline and often a different award amount.
Note the two-stage deadline pattern used by Radboud University: the application must be submitted, then made complete, and documents cannot be added after the completeness deadline.
Assemble proof of English proficiency early enough to be filed before the institutional completeness deadline, even if your admission is already secured.
Build a realistic financing plan for the full nominal duration of the programme and be ready to evidence it in the institution's own format.
If you are at Radboud University, apply for the Radboud Scholarship Programme in the same cycle â€” the NLS cannot be awarded on its own.
common_rejection_risks: Applying to a programme that does not participate in the NL Scholarship at that institution.
Missing the institutional deadline: the central 1 November opening date is not the deadline, and each institution sets its own.
Submitting after the completeness deadline â€” Radboud University states incomplete applications will not be considered for scholarship selection.
Being ineligible for statutory or lower EU/EEA tuition fees despite holding a non-EEA passport.
Having a Dutch degree or prior Dutch enrolment, which disqualifies under the central criteria.
At Utrecht University, a financial plan that does not cover the full nominal duration of the programme, or that the institution judges not realistic.
Submitting late in the window: Utrecht University warns that between 27 January and 1 February, incomplete or incorrect information cannot be updated or supplemented.
Assuming admission to the programme means scholarship selection â€” the two are separate processes.
estimated_uncovered_costs: The statutory tuition fee for a non-EEA student, minus whatever the institution's award tier covers.
Living costs for the full programme duration â€” explicitly not covered by the scholarship.
Visa and residence permit costs.
Health insurance and any required supplementary insurance.
Travel to and from the Netherlands.
Books, materials, course-related travel and other study-related expenses.
document_audit: Statement of Financial Resources: download the institution's own PDF form and complete every field; Utrecht University expects coverage of the full nominal duration of the programme, not just year one.
Proof of English proficiency: file before the institutional completeness deadline; Radboud University explicitly recommends this against the 14 February 2027 date.

OSIRIS application: check every uploaded document is correct, legible and complete, because the institution returns applications with incorrect, illegible or missing documents and those defects are not curable after the completeness deadline.
Keep file names and formats consistent with your institution's upload rules, which are set on the institution's page and were not published centrally.
Retain proof of submission: the submitted date, not the completed date, is what triggers the first deadline in the Radboud pattern.

records.description: The Royal Society Career Development Fellowship is a four-year postdoctoral research fellowship supporting early career scientists from underrepresented backgrounds to establish research in a UK institution. Applicants can apply for up to £703,800 over four years, covering a contribution to the Research Fellow's salary and associated on-costs (at 80%), directly allocated costs (at 80%), and research expenses (at 100%). Relocation and visa costs for the applicant and dependants can be requested in addition to the grant cap. The scheme is funded by the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade (BIST) and Royal Society charitable funds, with a variant funding research directly relevant to dementia in partnership with the Alzheimer's Society.
records.best_fit: Researchers who self-identify as being from a Black heritage background, including mixed Black background, with fewer than 24 months of postdoctoral experience, who meet the UK connection requirement and want a four-year postdoctoral fellowship in the UK.
records.eligibility_summary: Self-identify as being from a Black heritage background, have a UK connection (national, education or a UK postdoc position), hold or be completing a PhD with less than 24 months postdoctoral experience, and work within the Royal Society's natural sciences remit.
eligibility: You self-identify as being from a Black heritage, including mixed Black background.

You are a UK national or you have completed a part of your education in the UK through your Undergraduate, Master's or PhD degree studies or you hold/have held a postdoctoral researcher position in the UK.
You have a PhD, or will have one by the time the funding starts, but have less than 24 months post-doctoral experience.

Your research is within the Royal Society's remit of natural sciences, which includes but is not limited to, biological research and biomedical sciences, chemistry, engineering, mathematics and physics.
Both UK and non-UK domiciled researchers who wish to conduct their research in the UK are eligible.
Applicants can be of any nationality and those requiring a visa are eligible to apply for a Global Talent Visa under the fast-track process of endorsement.

records.notes: This scheme is currently offered as a pilot with researchers from Black heritage backgrounds; if successful, the pilot may be broadened to other underrepresented groups. It is a postdoctoral fellowship for research in the UK, not a degree programme, so it does not pay tuition. Salary and directly allocated costs are paid at 80%, so the host institution must cover part of the cost base. The Royal Society states undergraduate, Master's and PhD students cannot apply for Royal Society funding.

records.name: Humboldt Research Fellowship
records.region: Germany (host research institution)
records.duration: Postdocs: 6 to 24 months, divided into up to three stays within three years. Experienced researchers: 6 to 18 months, divided into up to three stays within three years.
records.deadline: Rolling in three calls per year, each opening approximately eight months before the selection meeting and closing when 800 applications are received. The next call opens on 15 November 2026 for the July 2027 selection meeting, with the earliest possible fellowship start in September 2027. The current call has reached the maximum of 800 applications and no new applications can be created.
records.application_period: Three calls per year: opened 15 March 2026 (selection meeting November 2026, earliest start February 2027), 15 July 2026 (selection meeting March 2027, earliest start May 2027), and next on 15 November 2026 (selection meeting July 2027, earliest start September 2027). Each call closes automatically once 800 applications are received.
records.description: The Humboldt Research Fellowship sponsors researchers with above-average qualifications from across the globe to conduct their own research at a German host institution. For postdocs the monthly fellowship amount is €3,000 and for experienced researchers €3,600, plus additional benefits. On top of the fellowship amount the Foundation provides family benefits for children and partners, subsidies for private full health insurance, and travel expense allowances, as well as personal support throughout the sponsorship. The host institute generally receives an allowance for research costs of €800 per month for natural sciences and engineering, or €500 for humanities and social sciences.
records.best_fit: Non-German postdoctoral researchers who completed their doctorate within the last four years (or experienced researchers within twelve years) and need a 6-24 month research stay in Germany.
records.eligibility_summary: Non-German national with a doctorate completed within the last four years (postdoc track) or twelve years (experienced researcher track), no more than 90 days in Germany in the 18 months before applying, with a German host providing a mentoring agreement and a confirmation of research facilities.
eligibility: Postdocs: did you complete your doctorate - or equivalent academic qualification - during the last four years?
Experienced researchers: did you complete your doctorate - or equivalent academic qualification - during the last twelve years?
Postdocs: have you been published in academic journals and by publishing houses that are reviewed according to international standards?

Experienced researchers: is your academic profile substantiated by an extensive list of publications including important papers in which you acted as thematic lead, and do you hold a leadership role commensurate with your career level (for example assistant professor, lecturer, head of an independent research group or higher)?

If a doctorate in your field or country of origin is not possible or uncommon, you can still apply up to 16 years after completing your master's or other postgraduate degree provided you have a publication record commensurate with your career level.

You are not a German national. If you are a German national, or if you obtained your university entrance qualification and university degree, or your university degree and your doctorate, in Germany, you can apply if you have lived and worked abroad for more than ten years and intend to continue doing so long-term. Have you lived and worked abroad for more than five years? You can still apply if there is a strong connection to your current country of residence (permanent employment, additional citizenship etc.).
For your application to be successful, you may not have lived in Germany for longer than a total of 90 days within the 18-month period prior to submitting your application.

A researcher from an academic institution of your choice in Germany will provide you with a mentoring agreement and written confirmation that research facilities are available, and will compile a detailed review for you.

You can provide two expert reviews. For postdocs: your doctoral supervisor and one other researcher - outside of your institute, if possible. For experienced researchers: important collaborative partners and/or researchers at your own institute as well as other institutes - outside your country of origin, if possible.

Natural sciences and engineering: you must have a good knowledge of German or English. Humanities, social sciences and medicine: you must have a good knowledge of German if this is necessary for conducting your research successfully; otherwise good knowledge of English will suffice.
You may not apply for the Humboldt Research Fellowship if you have already received sponsorship directly from the Humboldt Foundation (research fellowship or award).

Your host will receive a link to upload a host's statement and mentoring agreement; the application is only forwarded to the Foundation once the host has uploaded all necessary documents
Applications that fail to include important documents or information, or that diverge substantially from the specifications, will be formally rejected without further review
records.english_requirement: Natural sciences and engineering: you must have a good knowledge of German or English. Humanities, social sciences and medicine: you must have a good knowledge of German if this is necessary for conducting your research successfully; otherwise, good knowledge of English will suffice. No language certificate is required if English or German is your native language. An English language certificate is not required if you have worked in an English-speaking country for several years.

The application is only received by the Foundation once all documents, including the host's, have been submitted
records.selection_notes: The decision to award research fellowships is taken by a selection committee consisting of 60-70 researchers from various fields. Applications are academically evaluated by a peer review process based on: academic career and academic record to date (mobility, determination, thematic scope, academic productivity); quality of the key publications named in the application; originality and innovative potential of your proposed research; your future potential; and your independent research profile (for experienced researchers). The assessment also considers the individual life journey and educational background in terms of equal opportunities and accessibility. The Foundation expects 20-25% of the applications received to be approved.
records.notes: The current call has reached the maximum of 800 applications, so no new applications can be created at present; the next call opens on 15 November 2026. Applicants who have already started an application can save and continue working on it but cannot submit until the next application round opens. Applications are forwarded to the Foundation only after the host has uploaded their documents, so the host's speed determines your effective submission. Applicant who has already worked in Germany for 12 months or more should look for a new academic environment; applications involving returning to the doctoral supervisor or mentor of a longer postdoctoral stay are generally rejected. Individuals with whom you are in a close personal or familial relationship cannot be selected as hosts. In the case of unanimously rejected applications you must wait a minimum of 18 months before re-applying. Decisions cannot be appealed.

records.description: The Wellcome Early-Career Award funds early-career researchers from any discipline who are ready to develop their research identity and lead their own independent research programme. The award provides the total cost of the grantholder's salary for the entire grant period, determined by the administering organisation, plus up to £400,000 for research expenses. Certain costs sit outside the £400,000 limit, including overheads, overseas allowances, adjustment support, and the cost of macaques purchased from the MRC Centre for Macaques. Staff salaries are funded up to the equivalent of a 36-month full-time post, and no studentships are provided on this award.
records.best_fit: Researchers with a completed PhD (or equivalent) and no more than three years of postdoctoral experience, from any discipline, based at an eligible UK, Republic of Ireland or eligible LMIC organisation, whose work has potential to improve human life, health and wellbeing.
records.funding_period: up to, over the award duration (usually 5 years)
records.eligibility_summary: Early-career researcher with a passed PhD viva or at least four years' equivalent research experience, no more than three years of postdoctoral experience, at least 80% of research time on the project, based at an eligible administering organisation.
eligibility: You should be able to demonstrate the ability to conduct independent, original research that makes a meaningful contribution to knowledge, achieved through completion of a PhD or equivalent higher research degree (you must have passed your thesis defence by the date you submit your application), or through at least four years' research experience equivalent to a PhD.

Any periods of research undertaken during an undergraduate or Master's degree are not counted as equivalent research experience, and you must not have started a PhD or equivalent higher research degree if relying on the experience route.

You may have some postdoctoral experience in your proposed field of study, but no more than three years at the date of submission unless you can demonstrate how other factors have impacted on your research career.

You must be able to contribute at least 80% of your research time in support of the project proposed in the award, and should not spend more than 20% of your time on non-research related activities; if you are in a clinical craft speciality you may spend up to 40% of your time on clinical duties.

If you are a health professional and want to continue with clinical activities, you must be registered with, and be licensed by, the relevant professional regulator in the country you intend to work in.

Your administering organisation must be in the UK, the Republic of Ireland, or a low- or middle-income country apart from India and mainland China; the organisation must be not-for-profit and can be a higher education institution, research institute or healthcare organisation.

Your sponsor must be an individual at your administering organisation holding an established post (or an honorary academic appointment) for the duration of the award, and must guarantee the space and resources you will need from the start date to the end date of the award.
You should also identify a mentor for the period of your award with a track record in training and mentorship; your sponsor can also be your mentor. Sponsors and mentors are not paid for their input.
Coapplicants are not accepted.
You may only have one application under consideration as a lead applicant at any one time for the Early Career Award, Career Development Award and Discovery Award schemes.

Your research must fit within what Wellcome supports in Discovery Research and have the potential to improve human life, health and wellbeing; it can be in any discipline including STEM, experimental medicine, humanities and social science, clinical/allied health sciences and public health.

records.selection_notes: Applications are assessed through Wellcome's shortlisting Advisory Groups and then peer review. The same project may be submitted for consideration a maximum of two times across all Wellcome funding schemes and themed funding calls, and resubmissions must include significant changes demonstrating clear development of the original proposal. If your application scores in the lowest levels at the shortlisting meeting you will not be permitted to resubmit. If unsuccessful with an Early-Career Award, you may submit one further application for the same project to any Wellcome scheme, provided you still meet the eligibility criteria.
records.notes: Location eligibility is changing on 29 October 2026: from that date Wellcome will only accept applications from lead applicants based at eligible administering organisations in the UK and low- and middle-income countries in Africa, South Asia and South-East Asia, so an application submitted in October 2026 from a Republic of Ireland or a Latin American organisation would not be accepted under the new rule. You can only hold one of these awards and Wellcome does not offer renewals. No studentships are provided on this award. You cannot apply if you hold or have accepted an equivalent award at this career stage, or if you have an existing tenured salaried post for the duration of the award (unless based in a low- or middle-income country). You cannot apply if you intend to carry out activities that involve the transfer of grant funds into mainland China. Total resubmission of the same project is capped at two times across all Wellcome schemes. Overheads are not paid to UK research organisations that already receive core funding for overheads.

records.description: The JJ/WBGSP is a fully funded master's scholarship for mid-career professionals from listed World Bank developing countries who are already admitted to one of a fixed set of participating development-related master's programmes. For the 2027 cycle the World Bank states that a scholarship provides tuition, a monthly subsistence allowance to cover all living expenses while on campus, economy class round-trip airfare, basic medical insurance obtained through the university, and a US$600 travel allowance for each trip. The amount of the monthly subsistence allowance varies depending on the host country and is not published on the programme page. The Government of Japan solely funds the scholarship on an annual basis, and scholars commit to return to their home country after earning their degree.

records.selection_notes: Two qualified assessors independently review each eligible application and score it from 1 to 10 on four factors: quality of professional experience (30% weight), quality of professional recommendations (30% weight), quality of commitment to the applicant's home country (30% weight), and quality of education background (10% weight). The Secretariat uses the average of the two assessors plus a reasonably wide geographical distribution of awards, a reasonable distribution across gender, unusual circumstances or hardships, and giving scholarships to applicants who otherwise have limited access to financial resources for graduate studies abroad. Finalists go to the JJ/WBGSP Steering Committee, composed of members of the World Bank Board of Directors and World Bank management, for approval.
records.notes: Not eligible if admitted to a non-participating programme: the World Bank states explicitly that if you are not admitted to one of the participating master's programs you are not eligible to apply for a JJ/WBGSP scholarship in 2027. The scholarship does NOT cover visa application costs, expenses to bring and/or support family members, extra-curricular courses or training, courses below the minimum credits required for the degree, language training not provided by the graduate program, additional travel during the study program, research or supplementary educational materials, field trips, workshops, seminars or internships, educational equipment such as computers, and the resident permit fee. The scholarship may only supplement, and does not duplicate, any other source of financial support; if you hold another award you must send those documents to the JJ/WBGSP Secretariat. Scholars commit to return to their home country after earning their degree. Declining an earlier offer, or receiving the scholarship and failing to graduate, permanently bars reapplication. The 2026 window for Japanese nationals closed on Friday 17 April 2026, so only the 2027 developing-country-national cycle is live.

records.description: Under the 2026 cycle UNESCO and the Government of Japan award 10 fellowships to young researchers from Africa, Small Island Developing States, Ukraine and Turkiye to carry out postgraduate research in a Japanese university or research institution. Selected fellows may receive a fellowship grant of up to US$10,000, provided as a lump-sum contribution intended to cover costs directly related to the approved research stay in Japan. The grant may cover international and domestic travel for the approved itinerary, accommodation, medical insurance, personal subsistence in Japan including meals, local transportation and incidental expenses, and other research-related expenses where applicable. records.notes: Only 10 fellowships are awarded in the 2026 cycle, and only applications nominated by your National Commission are accepted, so the national shortlist is the binding gate. The fellowship grant is a lump sum capped at US$10,000, not a line-itemed scholarship, and the cost of the mandatory medical insurance is deducted from the total before disbursement, so the amount actually received is below the ceiling. The grant does NOT cover tuition fees, the purchase of equipment including computers, publication costs, or participation in conferences, unless such participation can be clearly justified as an integral part of the research and makes a direct and significant contribution to the project. official_details.description: Established in 2001 under the Japanese Funds-in-Trust for the Capacity-Building of Human Resources, the UNESCO/Japan Young Researchers' Fellowships Programme, also known as the UNESCO/Keizo Obuchi Research Fellowships Programme, is a long-standing initiative supported by the Government of Japan to strengthen research capacities and promote international knowledge exchange in areas aligned with UNESCO's mandate. Under the 2026 cycle, UNESCO and the Government of Japan will award 10 fellowships to highly qualified young researchers from Africa, Small Island Developing States, Ukraine and Turkiye. The fellowships support innovative and high-quality postgraduate research related to heritage conservation and management, sustainable development and artificial intelligence, with particular attention to interdisciplinary research connecting these themes with social, ethical, governance and contextual dimensions. Selected fellows may receive a fellowship grant of up to US$10,000, provided as a lump-sum contribution intended to cover costs directly related to the approved research stay in Japan. Since its establishment, the Programme has enabled 300 young researchers from 100 countries around the world to pursue postgraduate research.
